questions.q: Which pairing correctly matches the seam on the outside of the scrotum with the wall that divides it on the inside?
questions.why: The scrotum is a pouch of skin and subcutaneous tissue that holds the testes. A raphe, a ridge that looks like a seam, runs down the middle of its outer surface. Inside, the scrotal septum divides the pouch into two compartments, one for each testis, and the raphe on the surface marks where that septum lies underneath.
notes: This reverses the two terms. The raphe is the visible seam on the skin and the septum is the partition inside, so a student who knows both words but mixes up surface and deep tends to pick this.

The dartos and cremaster are the two muscles that adjust the scrotum and testes, not a surface seam or a dividing wall. Pick them if the question asked which muscles help control the temperature of the testes.
The tunica vaginalis and tunica albuginea are coverings of each testis, not markings of the scrotum. Choose them if the question asked for the serous membrane and the fibrous capsule around a testis.
Correct. The raphe is the seam on the skin, and the scrotal septum is the internal wall between the two testes.

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the tunica vaginalis and the tunica albuginea of the testis?
options: The vaginalis is a serous membrane; the albuginea is a fibrous capsule
The vaginalis divides the testis; the albuginea lines its tubules
The vaginalis is a fibrous capsule; the albuginea is a serous membrane
Both are layers of smooth muscle found in the scrotal wall
questions.why: The tunica vaginalis is a serous membrane, a thin double-layered sheet derived from the peritoneum, and it partly covers the front and sides of each testis. Deep to it, the tunica albuginea is a tough white capsule of dense connective tissue that wraps the testis directly. The albuginea also sends walls inward that divide the testis into a few hundred wedge-shaped lobules.
notes: Correct. The vaginalis is the serous outer covering, and the albuginea is the fibrous capsule beneath it.
The tunica albuginea, not the vaginalis, divides the testis into lobules, and neither tunica lines the seminiferous tubules. This statement scrambles which structure does which job.
This swaps the two layers. The albuginea is the fibrous capsule and the vaginalis is the serous membrane from the peritoneum, which is the mix-up to watch for because the names look alike.
Neither tunica is muscle. The smooth muscle of the scrotal wall is the dartos, so pick smooth muscle if the question asked what wrinkles the scrotal skin.
questions.answerText: The vaginalis is a serous membrane; the albuginea is a fibrous capsule

questions.q: Where are the sustentacular (Sertoli) cells of the testis located?
options: In the spaces between the tubules
In the wall of the epididymis
questions.why: Sustentacular cells, also called Sertoli cells, form the lining of the seminiferous tubules, the coiled tubes where sperm are produced. They surround and nourish the developing sperm, and tight connections between neighboring Sertoli cells form the blood-testis barrier, which separates the developing sperm from the blood supply. The name sustentacular means supporting, which matches their job.
notes: Correct. Sertoli cells line the seminiferous tubules and support the developing sperm.
The spaces between the tubules hold the interstitial (Leydig) cells, which produce testosterone. Pick this location if the question asked where the interstitial cells sit.

The epididymis is the coiled duct on the testis where sperm are stored and gain the ability to move. It would be the answer if the question asked where sperm mature after leaving the testis, not where the support cells of sperm production are found.
The tunica albuginea is the white fibrous capsule around the testis, not a layer of cells inside the tubules. Choose it if the question asked which capsule divides the testis into lobules.

questions.q: What do the interstitial (Leydig) cells of the testis produce?
questions.why: The interstitial cells, also called Leydig cells, sit in the spaces between the seminiferous tubules and produce testosterone, the main male sex hormone. This is why the testes are said to do two jobs: the tubules make sperm, and the cells between the tubules make hormones. The word interstitial simply means located in the spaces between other structures.
notes: Alkaline mucus comes from the bulbourethral glands, which lubricate the urethra and neutralize traces of urine. Choose it if the question asked what the glands below the prostate secrete.
A fructose-rich alkaline fluid comes from the seminal vesicles, the paired glands behind the bladder. It would be the answer if the question asked which secretion makes up the largest share of semen.
Correct. Leydig cells between the tubules produce testosterone.
Sperm are produced inside the seminiferous tubules, not by the cells between them. Pick sperm if the question asked what the seminiferous tubules make.

questions.q: Which part of a sperm cell is packed with mitochondria that power its movement?
questions.why: The middle piece is the part of the tail just behind the neck, and it is packed with mitochondria, the organelles that make ATP, the energy molecule cells run on. That energy drives the whipping motion of the rest of the tail. In order, the tail runs from the neck to the middle piece, then the principal piece, and finally the end piece.
notes: Correct. The middle piece holds the mitochondria that supply energy for swimming.
The acrosome is the enzyme-filled cap over the head that helps the sperm get through the layers around the oocyte. It would be the answer if the question asked which part holds those enzymes.
The end piece is the thin, tapering last part of the tail. Choose it if the question asked for the terminal portion of the tail.
The head holds the nucleus with its 23 chromosomes, the genetic material the sperm delivers. Pick it if the question asked where the chromosomes are carried.

questions.q: Inside the testis, sperm move from the seminiferous tubules into a network of small channels before they pass to the epididymis. What is this network called?
questions.why: The rete testis is a network of small channels near the back of the testis that collects sperm from the seminiferous tubules. From the rete testis, sperm pass through a few small efferent ducts into the head of the epididymis. The word rete means net, which describes this mesh of channels.
notes: Correct. The rete testis collects sperm from the tubules and passes them toward the epididymis.

The tunica vaginalis is the serous membrane, derived from the peritoneum, that partly covers the outside of the testis. It carries no sperm, so choose it only if the question asked about a covering of the testis.

The pampiniform plexus is also a network, but it is a network of veins in the spermatic cord that drains the testis. Pick it if the question asked which venous network surrounds the testicular artery in the cord.

The spermatic cord is the bundle outside the testis that holds the ductus deferens, vessels, nerves, and cremaster muscle. It is the answer for what passes through the inguinal canal, not for channels inside the testis.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the epididymis?
options: A short duct through the prostate that empties into the urethra
A pair of glands behind the bladder that make fructose-rich fluid
A comma-shaped duct on the back of the testis that stores sperm
A muscular duct in the spermatic cord that carries sperm upward
questions.why: The epididymis is a comma-shaped, tightly coiled duct that sits along the posterior side of each testis. Sperm that leave the testis are stored here and gain the ability to move, a process called maturation. It is the first duct of the male duct system, linking sperm production in the testis to the ductus deferens that carries sperm away.
notes: This describes the ejaculatory duct, formed where the ductus deferens meets the seminal vesicle duct. It would be correct if the question asked which duct empties into the prostatic urethra.
This describes the seminal vesicles, which add an alkaline, fructose-rich fluid that is the largest share of semen. Choose it if the question asked about the seminal vesicles.
Correct. The epididymis is the comma-shaped duct on the posterior testis where sperm are stored and mature.

This describes the ductus deferens (vas deferens), which carries sperm from the epididymis up out of the scrotum inside the spermatic cord. Pick this statement if the question asked about the ductus deferens.
questions.answerText: A comma-shaped duct on the back of the testis that stores sperm

questions.q: The ductus deferens widens just before it joins the duct of the seminal vesicle. What is this widened end called?
questions.why: After passing through the inguinal canal, the ductus deferens runs into the pelvis, crosses over the ureter, and travels down the back of the urinary bladder. Its last stretch widens into the ampulla, a word that means flask. The ampulla then joins the duct of the seminal vesicle to form the ejaculatory duct.
notes: The rete testis is the network of channels inside the testis that collects sperm from the seminiferous tubules. It sits at the start of the route, not at the end of the ductus deferens.
Correct. The ampulla is the widened end of the ductus deferens.
The bulb is part of the root of the penis, the enlarged base of the corpus spongiosum. Pick it if the question asked which structures make up the attached root of the penis.

The crus (plural crura) is the anchored base of each corpus cavernosum, also in the root of the penis. It would be the answer if the question asked how the dorsal erectile columns attach to the pelvic bones.

questions.q: Which structure travels within the spermatic cord?
questions.why: The spermatic cord is the bundle that suspends each testis and passes through the inguinal canal. It contains the ductus deferens, the testicular artery, the pampiniform plexus of veins that drains the testis, nerves, lymphatic vessels, and the cremaster muscle. The pampiniform plexus wraps around the testicular artery, which helps cool the blood flowing down to the testis.
notes: Correct. The pampiniform plexus is the network of veins in the spermatic cord.

The ejaculatory duct lies deep in the pelvis, where the ductus deferens meets the seminal vesicle duct, and it empties into the prostatic urethra. Pick it if the question asked which short duct passes through the prostate.

The bulbourethral glands are pea-sized glands below the prostate that release mucus into the urethra. They would be the answer for glands beside the membranous urethra, not for something inside the cord.
The seminal vesicles are glands on the back of the bladder, deep in the pelvis and outside the cord. Choose them if the question asked which gland contributes the largest share of semen.

questions.q: Each ejaculatory duct empties into which region of the urethra?
questions.why: Each ejaculatory duct forms where the ampulla of the ductus deferens joins the duct of a seminal vesicle. The short duct then passes through the prostate and opens into the prostatic urethra, the first region of the male urethra just below the bladder. From that point on, sperm share the urethra with the urinary tract.
notes: The external urethral orifice is the opening at the tip of the penis where semen and urine leave the body. It is the end of the route, not where the ejaculatory ducts join it.
The spongy urethra is the longest region, running through the penis inside the corpus spongiosum. Choose it if the question asked where the bulbourethral glands release their mucus.

The membranous urethra is the short middle region that passes through the floor of the pelvis between the prostate and the penis. It comes after the prostatic urethra, so pick it if the question asked which region sperm enter after leaving the prostate.
Correct. The ejaculatory ducts open into the prostatic urethra.

questions.q: Which set lists the three male accessory glands?
questions.why: The male accessory glands are the paired seminal vesicles, the single prostate, and the paired bulbourethral glands. Each adds fluid to the sperm as they move through the ducts, and the mixture of sperm and these fluids is semen. They are called accessory because they support reproduction without producing the gametes themselves.
notes: Correct. These three glands add the fluid portion of semen.

The epididymis is part of the duct system, the coiled duct on the testis where sperm are stored and mature. It belongs in a list of the male ducts with the ductus deferens, ejaculatory ducts, and urethra.
Interstitial cells are hormone-producing cells between the seminiferous tubules, not a gland that adds fluid to semen. Choose them if the question asked which cells produce testosterone.
The testes are the gonads, the primary reproductive organs that make sperm and hormones, so they are not accessory glands. Pick the testes if the question asked for the male gonads.

questions.q: Which description matches the fluid made by the seminal vesicles?
options: Milky, and helps sperm stay active
questions.why: The seminal vesicles are paired glands on the back of the urinary bladder. Their fluid is alkaline, meaning slightly basic, and rich in fructose, a sugar the sperm use for energy. This fluid makes up the largest share of semen.
notes: Correct. Seminal vesicle fluid is alkaline and rich in fructose.

Testosterone is a hormone released into the blood by the interstitial cells of the testis, not part of any accessory gland fluid. Students who mix up the hormone-making cells with the fluid-making glands tend to pick this.
A milky fluid that helps sperm stay active comes from the prostate, the single gland around the urethra below the bladder. Pick this description if the question asked about prostate fluid.
Clear, alkaline mucus comes from the bulbourethral glands, which lubricate the urethra and neutralize traces of urine. Choose it if the question asked about the glands below the prostate.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the prostate?
options: A pair of glands behind the bladder that make fructose-rich fluid
A pair of pea-sized glands that release mucus into the urethra
A single coiled duct on the testis where sperm are stored
A single gland below the bladder that surrounds the urethra
questions.why: The prostate is a single gland, about the size of a walnut, that sits just below the urinary bladder and wraps around the first part of the urethra, the prostatic urethra. It adds a milky fluid that helps sperm stay active. Because the urethra passes straight through it, an enlarged prostate can squeeze the urethra and slow urine flow.
notes: This describes the seminal vesicles, the paired glands on the back of the bladder. Pick this statement if the question asked which glands supply the largest share of semen.
This describes the bulbourethral (Cowper's) glands, which sit below the prostate. Choose it if the question asked which glands lubricate the urethra with alkaline mucus.
This describes the epididymis, a duct rather than a gland. It would be correct if the question asked where sperm are stored and gain the ability to move.
Correct. The prostate is one gland below the bladder wrapped around the prostatic urethra.
questions.answerText: A single gland below the bladder that surrounds the urethra

questions.q: What does the mucus from the bulbourethral glands do?
options: Keeps sperm active with a milky fluid
Lubricates the urethra and neutralizes leftover urine
Supplies the fructose that sperm use for energy
Shields developing sperm from the blood supply
questions.why: The bulbourethral glands, also called Cowper's glands, are pea-sized glands just below the prostate. Before ejaculation they release a clear, alkaline mucus into the spongy urethra, where it lubricates the passage and neutralizes traces of acidic urine. Alkaline means slightly basic, the opposite of acidic.
notes: A milky fluid that keeps sperm active comes from the prostate. Choose this if the question asked what the gland around the prostatic urethra secretes.
Correct. Bulbourethral mucus lubricates the urethra and neutralizes acidic urine.
Fructose for energy comes from the seminal vesicles, the paired glands on the back of the bladder. Pick this if the question asked about seminal vesicle fluid.

Shielding developing sperm from the blood is the job of the sustentacular (Sertoli) cells, whose tight connections form the blood-testis barrier. That is a role inside the testis, not a gland secretion.
questions.answerText: Lubricates the urethra and neutralizes leftover urine

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the corpora cavernosa and the corpus spongiosum?
options: The two cavernosa are dorsal and hold the urethra; the one spongiosum is ventral
The two cavernosa are dorsal; the one spongiosum is ventral and holds the urethra
The two cavernosa are ventral and hold the urethra; the one spongiosum is dorsal
The one cavernosum is dorsal; the two spongiosa are ventral and hold the urethra
questions.why: The penis has three columns of erectile tissue, spongy tissue that fills with blood during an erection. The paired corpora cavernosa run side by side along the dorsal side, and the single corpus spongiosum runs along the ventral side and surrounds the spongy urethra. The corpus spongiosum also expands at the tip to form the glans penis.
notes: The counts and positions are right, but the urethra runs through the corpus spongiosum, not the cavernosa. That is why the penile part of the urethra is called the spongy urethra.
Correct. Two dorsal cavernosa and one ventral spongiosum that carries the spongy urethra.
This flips the positions. The cavernosa are dorsal, and the spongiosum is the ventral column, so the urethra is not inside the cavernosa.
This reverses the counts. There are two corpora cavernosa and only one corpus spongiosum, which is easy to remember because cavernosa is the plural form.
questions.answerText: The two cavernosa are dorsal; the one spongiosum is ventral and holds the urethra

questions.q: Semen is a mixture of sperm and gland fluids. Which structure supplies the sperm cells themselves?
questions.why: Semen has four sources. The sperm cells are made in the seminiferous tubules of the testes, while the fluid comes from the three accessory glands: the seminal vesicles, the prostate, and the bulbourethral glands. Only the seminiferous tubules produce sperm; every other structure on the route stores, carries, or adds fluid.
notes: The bulbourethral glands add a small amount of alkaline mucus that lubricates the urethra. They would be the answer if the question asked which glands lie below the prostate.
Correct. Sperm are produced in the seminiferous tubules of the testes.
The seminal vesicles add an alkaline, fructose-rich fluid, the largest share of semen, but no sperm. Pick them if the question asked which gland contributes the most fluid.
The prostate adds a milky fluid that helps sperm stay active, but no sperm. Choose it if the question asked which gland surrounds the urethra below the bladder.

questions.q: What is the skin-covered pouch that holds the testes outside the body cavity?
questions.why: The scrotum is a pouch of skin and subcutaneous tissue that holds the testes outside the abdominopelvic cavity. This position keeps the testes a few degrees cooler than the body core, which sperm production requires. A raphe marks the middle of its surface, and an internal scrotal septum separates the two testes.
notes: Correct. The scrotum is the pouch that holds the testes.
The perineum is the whole diamond-shaped region between the thighs, not the pouch itself. Choose it if the question asked for the region that contains the external genitalia and the anus.
The spermatic cord is the bundle that suspends each testis and carries the ductus deferens and testicular vessels. It hangs inside the scrotum but is not the pouch that holds the testes.
The prepuce is the foreskin, the loose fold of skin over the glans penis. Pick it if the question asked which fold of skin covers the tip of the penis.

questions.q: Which structures are the male gonads, the primary reproductive organs?
questions.why: The testes are the male gonads, the primary reproductive organs. They produce the gametes (sperm) inside the seminiferous tubules and secrete hormones, mainly testosterone, from the interstitial cells. Every other male reproductive structure either carries sperm, adds fluid to them, or helps deliver them.
notes: The seminal vesicles are accessory glands that add a fructose-rich fluid to semen. Pick them if the question asked which gland makes the largest share of semen.
The prostate is an accessory gland around the urethra below the bladder. It would be the answer if the question asked which gland is enlarged in benign prostatic hyperplasia.
Correct. The testes are the male gonads.
The epididymis is a duct on the back of the testis where sperm are stored and mature. Choose it if the question asked where sperm gain the ability to move.

questions.q: Where inside the testis are sperm produced?
questions.why: Sperm are produced in the seminiferous tubules, long, tightly coiled tubes packed into the lobules of each testis. The sustentacular (Sertoli) cells lining these tubules nourish the developing sperm. Once formed, sperm leave the tubules and move on to be stored and matured in the epididymis.
notes: The tunica albuginea is the fibrous capsule of the testis that divides it into lobules. Pick it if the question asked for the capsule, not the site of sperm production.
The rete testis is the network of channels that collects sperm after they leave the seminiferous tubules. It would be the answer if the question asked where sperm go next inside the testis.
Correct. The seminiferous tubules are the only sperm-producing structures.
The interstitial cells sit between the tubules and produce testosterone, not sperm. Choose them if the question asked which cells of the testis make hormones.

questions.q: Which organ lies along the posterior side of each testis?
questions.why: The epididymis is a comma-shaped, coiled duct that hugs the posterior side of each testis inside the scrotum. Sperm leave the testis and enter the epididymis, where they are stored and gain the ability to move. Its position right against the testis makes it the first stop after sperm are produced.
notes: Correct. The epididymis sits on the posterior side of each testis.
The seminal vesicles lie on the back of the urinary bladder, far from the testis. Choose them if the question asked which gland lies behind the bladder.
The bulbourethral glands are small glands below the prostate beside the membranous urethra. They would be the answer if the question asked which glands release mucus into the spongy urethra.
The prostate is a single gland deep in the pelvis, just below the bladder and around the urethra. Pick it if the question asked which gland surrounds the first part of the urethra.

questions.q: What is the white fibrous capsule of the testis called?
questions.why: The tunica albuginea is the tough white capsule of dense connective tissue that wraps each testis. Albuginea means white, which describes its color. It also sends walls inward that divide the testis into a few hundred lobules, each holding seminiferous tubules.
notes: Correct. The tunica albuginea is the fibrous capsule of the testis.
The corpus spongiosum is the erectile column of the penis that surrounds the spongy urethra. It would be the answer if the question asked which column forms the glans.

The tunica vaginalis is the serous membrane, derived from the peritoneum, that partly covers the testis outside the albuginea. Choose it if the question asked for the serous covering rather than the fibrous capsule.
The dartos is the smooth muscle layer of the scrotum that wrinkles the skin to reduce heat loss. Pick it if the question asked about the muscle in the scrotal wall.

questions.q: What is the enlarged, acorn-shaped tip of the penis called?
questions.why: The glans penis is the enlarged, acorn-shaped tip of the penis, and the word glans means acorn. It is an expansion of the corpus spongiosum, the erectile column that surrounds the urethra, so the external urethral orifice opens at its tip. In an uncircumcised male, the prepuce covers it.
notes: The prepuce is the foreskin, the loose fold of skin that covers the glans. It would be the answer if the question asked what is removed in circumcision.
Correct. The glans is the acorn-shaped tip of the penis.
The body, or shaft, is the free, movable portion between the root and the tip. Choose it if the question asked for the main length of the penis.
The root is the attached portion of the penis, containing the bulb and the crura. Pick it if the question asked which part anchors the penis to the body.

questions.q: What is the foreskin of the penis called?
questions.why: The prepuce, or foreskin, is the loose fold of skin that covers the glans penis. It is the structure removed in circumcision. Because it is loose, it can slide back to expose the glans.
notes: Correct. The prepuce is the foreskin.
The glans is the acorn-shaped tip that the prepuce covers. Pick it if the question asked for the tip of the penis itself.
The root is the attached portion of the penis that contains the bulb and the crura. Choose it if the question asked which part anchors the penis to the body.
The raphe is the seam-like ridge down the middle of the scrotum. It would be the answer if the question asked what marks the surface of the scrotum.

questions.q: Which cell is the male gamete?
questions.why: A gamete is a sex cell that carries half the usual number of chromosomes, 23 in humans, and joins with another gamete at fertilization. The male gamete is the sperm cell, made in the seminiferous tubules of the testes. The female gamete is the oocyte, the egg cell made in the ovary.
notes: Sertoli (sustentacular) cells line the seminiferous tubules and nourish developing sperm. They support sperm production but are not gametes, so pick them if the question asked which cells form the blood-testis barrier.
Correct. The sperm cell is the male gamete.
Leydig (interstitial) cells sit between the seminiferous tubules and produce testosterone. They are body cells of the testis, so choose them if the question asked which cells make the male hormone.
The oocyte is the female gamete, produced in the ovary. Pick it if the question asked for the female sex cell.

questions.q: Which male reproductive structure sits just below the urinary bladder and surrounds the urethra?
questions.why: The prostate is a single, walnut-sized gland just inferior to the urinary bladder. The first part of the urethra runs straight through it, which is why that region is called the prostatic urethra. The prostate adds a milky fluid to semen that helps sperm stay active.
notes: Correct. The prostate lies below the bladder and encircles the urethra.

The seminal vesicles lie on the posterior surface of the bladder, behind it rather than below it, and they do not surround the urethra. Pick them if the question asked which glands lie behind the bladder.
The epididymis is a duct on the back of the testis inside the scrotum, nowhere near the bladder. It would be the answer if the question asked where sperm are stored.
The bulbourethral glands are pea-sized glands farther down, below the prostate beside the membranous urethra. Choose them if the question asked which glands lie inferior to the prostate.

questions.q: Which bundle suspends each testis and carries the ductus deferens and the testicular vessels?
questions.why: The spermatic cord is the bundle that hangs each testis in the scrotum and runs up through the inguinal canal into the abdominal wall. It holds the ductus deferens, the testicular artery, the pampiniform plexus of veins, nerves, lymphatic vessels, and the cremaster muscle. Think of it as the cable that connects each testis to the body.
notes: Correct. The spermatic cord suspends the testis and carries its duct, vessels, and nerves.
The ejaculatory duct is a short duct deep in the pelvis where the ductus deferens meets the seminal vesicle duct. Choose it if the question asked which duct empties into the prostatic urethra.
The inguinal canal is the passage through the anterior abdominal wall that the cord travels through, not the cord itself. Pick it if the question asked where an inguinal hernia occurs.
The tunica vaginalis is the serous membrane that partly covers each testis. It would be the answer if the question asked where fluid collects in a hydrocele.

questions.q: At the end of the male duct system, through which opening do sperm leave the body?
questions.why: The external urethral orifice is the opening at the tip of the glans penis, at the end of the spongy urethra. Semen leaves the body here, and so does urine, because the male urethra is shared by the reproductive and urinary systems. External means it opens to the outside of the body.
notes: Correct. Semen exits through the external urethral orifice at the tip of the penis.

The inguinal canal is a passage through the abdominal wall that carries the spermatic cord, not an exit from the body. It would be the answer if the question asked where an inguinal hernia pushes through.
The internal urethral orifice is where the urethra begins, at the outlet of the urinary bladder. Pick it if the question asked where urine leaves the bladder and enters the urethra.
The ejaculatory duct is an internal duct that empties into the prostatic urethra, much earlier in the route. Choose it if the question asked where the ductus deferens and seminal vesicle duct join.

questions.q: Which term names the diamond-shaped region between the thighs that contains the external genitalia and the anus?
questions.why: The perineum is the diamond-shaped region between the thighs, bounded by the pubic symphysis in front, the coccyx behind, and the ischial tuberosities on the sides. It contains the external genitalia and the anus. The membranous urethra passes through the floor of this region.
notes: The pubic region is the lower front of the trunk, just above the external genitalia. It would be the answer if the question asked for the regional term over the pubic bones.
The inguinal region is the groin, where the thigh meets the trunk, and it holds the inguinal canal. Choose it if the question asked where the spermatic cord passes through the abdominal wall.
The scrotum is the pouch that holds the testes, one structure within the perineum rather than the whole region. Pick it if the question asked for the sac that holds the testes.
Correct. The perineum is the region between the thighs that contains the external genitalia and anus.

questions.q: Which structure of the scrotum is a layer of smooth muscle?
questions.why: The dartos is a thin layer of smooth muscle in the wall of the scrotum, just under the skin. When it contracts, it wrinkles the scrotal skin and pulls it tighter, which reduces heat loss from the testes. Because it is smooth muscle, it works involuntarily.
notes: Correct. The dartos is the smooth muscle layer of the scrotum.
The scrotal raphe is the seam-like ridge on the surface of the scrotum, not a muscle layer. It would be the answer if the question asked what marks the midline of the scrotum.
The tunica vaginalis is a serous membrane covering the testis, not muscle. Choose it if the question asked which membrane is derived from the peritoneum.
The cremaster is the other scrotal muscle, but it is skeletal muscle, and it raises and lowers the testes. Pick it if the question asked which muscle is skeletal or which one lifts the testes.

questions.q: Which muscle raises and lowers the testes to adjust their temperature?
questions.why: The cremaster is a skeletal muscle that travels in the spermatic cord and loops around each testis. When it contracts, it pulls the testes up toward the warm body, and when it relaxes, the testes hang lower and cool off. This keeps them near the slightly cooler temperature that sperm production needs.
notes: Correct. The cremaster raises and lowers the testes.
The dartos is the smooth muscle of the scrotal wall that wrinkles the skin, but it does not lift the testes. Pick it if the question asked which muscle wrinkles the scrotum to reduce heat loss.
The myometrium is the smooth muscle layer of the uterus, a female structure. It would be the answer if the question asked which layer of the uterine wall contracts during labor.
The detrusor is the smooth muscle in the wall of the urinary bladder. Choose it if the question asked which muscle squeezes urine out of the bladder.

questions.q: Where in the testis are the interstitial (Leydig) cells found?
questions.why: Interstitial cells sit in the connective tissue spaces between the seminiferous tubules, which is exactly what interstitial means. They produce testosterone. Keeping the two cell types apart is easier if you link location to job: the cells inside the tubules support sperm production, and the cells between the tubules make hormone.
notes: The epididymis is the duct on the back of the testis where sperm are stored and mature, and it holds no Leydig cells. Choose it if the question asked where sperm gain the ability to move.

The cells lining the seminiferous tubules are the sustentacular (Sertoli) cells, which nourish developing sperm. Pick this location if the question asked about the cells that form the blood-testis barrier.
The prostate is an accessory gland below the bladder that adds a milky fluid to semen. It would be the answer if the question asked which gland surrounds the urethra.
Correct. Leydig cells lie between the seminiferous tubules.

questions.q: The ductus deferens is also known by which other name?
questions.why: The ductus deferens and the vas deferens are two names for the same duct. It carries sperm from the epididymis up out of the scrotum inside the spermatic cord, through the inguinal canal, and into the pelvis. The word deferens means carrying away.
notes: The efferent ducts are tiny ducts that carry sperm from the rete testis into the head of the epididymis. Choose them if the question asked how sperm leave the testis to enter the epididymis.
The ejaculatory duct is a separate, shorter duct formed where the ductus deferens meets the seminal vesicle duct. Pick it if the question asked which duct empties into the prostatic urethra.
The lactiferous ducts carry milk in the mammary gland, a female structure. They would be the answer if the question asked which ducts open at the nipple.
Correct. Vas deferens is another name for the ductus deferens.

questions.q: The ejaculatory duct is formed by the joining of which two structures?
options: Seminal vesicle duct and prostatic urethra
Ductus deferens and seminal vesicle duct
questions.why: On each side, the widened end of the ductus deferens (the ampulla) joins the duct of the seminal vesicle to form one ejaculatory duct. This is the point where sperm first mix with seminal vesicle fluid. The ejaculatory duct then passes through the prostate and empties into the prostatic urethra.
notes: The bulbourethral glands release mucus separately into the spongy urethra, farther down the route. They would be the answer if the question asked which glands lie below the prostate.
The prostatic urethra is where the ejaculatory duct ends, not one of the structures that forms it. Choose the urethra if the question asked where the ejaculatory duct empties.
Correct. The ductus deferens and the seminal vesicle duct merge to form the ejaculatory duct.

The epididymis does connect to the ductus deferens, but that junction is in the scrotum and simply continues the same tube. Pick this pair if the question asked which two ducts join at the tail of the epididymis.
questions.answerText: Ductus deferens and seminal vesicle duct

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the positions of the seminal vesicles and the prostate?
options: The seminal vesicles lie below the bladder; the prostate lies behind it
The seminal vesicles lie behind the bladder; the prostate lies below it
The seminal vesicles lie in the scrotum; the prostate lies below the bladder
Both glands lie side by side on the back wall of the bladder
questions.why: The seminal vesicles are a pair of elongated glands on the posterior surface of the urinary bladder. The prostate is a single gland just inferior to the bladder, wrapped around the first part of the urethra. The ducts of the seminal vesicles join the ductus deferens behind the bladder, and the resulting ejaculatory ducts then pass down through the prostate.
notes: This reverses the two positions. The prostate is the one below the bladder around the urethra, and the seminal vesicles are behind it, so this is the mirror-image mix-up.
Correct. Seminal vesicles are posterior to the bladder, and the prostate is inferior to it.

The seminal vesicles are deep in the pelvis, not in the scrotum. Students sometimes place them near the testes because of the word seminal, but the structures in the scrotum are the testes and epididymides.
Only the seminal vesicles sit on the back wall of the bladder. The prostate is below the bladder, which is why it can squeeze the urethra when it enlarges.
questions.answerText: The seminal vesicles lie behind the bladder; the prostate lies below it

questions.q: Which paired glands lie just below the prostate in the male?
questions.why: The bulbourethral glands, also called Cowper's glands, are a pair of pea-sized glands just inferior to the prostate, on either side of the membranous urethra. Their ducts open into the spongy urethra, where they release a clear alkaline mucus. Going from top to bottom, the order is bladder, prostate, then the bulbourethral glands.
notes: The greater vestibular glands are the female counterparts of the bulbourethral glands, found beside the vaginal opening. They would be the answer if the question asked which female glands lubricate the vestibule.
The testes hang in the scrotum outside the pelvis, far below and in front of the prostate. Choose them if the question asked for the male gonads.
The seminal vesicles lie behind the bladder, above and behind the prostate rather than below it. Pick them if the question asked which glands are on the posterior bladder wall.
Correct. The bulbourethral glands sit just below the prostate.

questions.q: Which paired columns of erectile tissue run along the dorsal side of the penis?
questions.why: The corpora cavernosa are the two larger columns of erectile tissue, and they run side by side along the dorsal side of the penis. Erectile tissue is a sponge of blood spaces that fills with blood during an erection. The word corpora is plural, which helps you remember there are two of them.
notes: Correct. The two corpora cavernosa run along the dorsal side.
The corpus spongiosum is the single ventral column that surrounds the spongy urethra. Pick it if the question asked which column holds the urethra or forms the glans.
The glans penis is the acorn-shaped tip, an expansion of the corpus spongiosum, not a paired column. Choose it if the question asked for the enlarged tip of the penis.
The prepuce is the foreskin, a fold of skin over the glans, not erectile tissue. It would be the answer if the question asked what is removed in circumcision.

questions.q: Which structure expands at the tip of the penis to form the glans?
questions.why: The corpus spongiosum is the single ventral column of erectile tissue that surrounds the spongy urethra. At the distal end of the penis it expands into the glans penis, which is why the urethra opens at the tip of the glans. At the other end, in the root, it expands into the bulb.
notes: The spongy urethra is the tube that runs inside the corpus spongiosum and opens at the tip. It carries urine and semen but does not form the glans, so pick it if the question asked which region of the urethra runs through the penis.
The corpora cavernosa are the two dorsal columns, and they end before the tip, capped by the glans. Pick them if the question asked which columns run along the dorsal side.
Correct. The glans is the expanded end of the corpus spongiosum.
The prepuce is the fold of skin covering the glans, not the tissue that forms it. Choose it if the question asked what the foreskin is called.

questions.q: The spermatic cord passes through which passage in the lower anterior abdominal wall?
questions.why: The inguinal canal is a short, slanted passage through the lower anterior abdominal wall in the groin. The spermatic cord runs through it, carrying the ductus deferens, testicular vessels, and nerves between the scrotum and the abdominopelvic cavity. Because it is a natural opening in the wall, it is also where an inguinal hernia can push through.
notes: The obturator foramen is the large opening in the hip bone, surrounded by the pubis and ischium, not a passage through the abdominal wall. Pick it if the question asked for the largest foramen of the hip bone.

The urethra is the tube that carries urine and semen out through the penis, not a passage through the abdominal wall. It would be the answer if the question asked which tube is shared by the urinary and reproductive systems.
Correct. The spermatic cord runs through the inguinal canal.

The ejaculatory duct is a short internal duct deep in the pelvis, formed where the ductus deferens meets the seminal vesicle duct. Choose it if the question asked which duct empties into the prostatic urethra.

questions.q: Which part of the penis is the attached portion anchored to the body?
questions.why: The root is the attached, internal portion of the penis, anchored in the perineum to the pelvic bones and the floor of the pelvis. It contains the bulb, the enlarged base of the corpus spongiosum, and the two crura, the anchored ends of the corpora cavernosa. The rest of the penis, the body and the glans, hangs free.
notes: Correct. The root is the attached portion of the penis.
The body, or shaft, is the free, movable portion of the penis. Pick it if the question asked for the part between the root and the tip.
The glans is the enlarged, acorn-shaped tip of the penis. Choose it if the question asked which part is an expansion of the corpus spongiosum at the distal end.
The prepuce is the foreskin over the glans. It would be the answer if the question asked which fold of skin is removed in circumcision.

questions.q: Which description best defines semen?
options: Fluid from the seminal vesicles alone
Sperm plus fluid from the accessory glands
A mix of sperm and urine in the urethra
Sperm stored in the epididymis before release
questions.why: Semen is the mixture of sperm and the fluids of the three accessory glands: the seminal vesicles, the prostate, and the bulbourethral glands. The sperm come from the seminiferous tubules, but most of the volume is gland fluid. These fluids nourish the sperm, give them a liquid to swim in, and help neutralize acid along the way.
notes: Seminal vesicle fluid is the largest single part of semen, but it is only one part. It contains no sperm on its own, so this would describe seminal vesicle secretion, not semen.
Correct. Semen is sperm combined with the fluids of the accessory glands.
Urine and semen share the male urethra, but semen is the mix of sperm and gland fluids, and urine is not part of it. Pick the urethra only if the question asked which tube carries both.
Sperm stored in the epididymis have not yet mixed with any gland fluid. This describes the stored sperm before ejaculation, not the final mixture called semen.
questions.answerText: Sperm plus fluid from the accessory glands

questions.q: Into which region of the urethra do the bulbourethral glands release their mucus?
questions.why: The bulbourethral glands sit on either side of the membranous urethra, just below the prostate, but their small ducts run forward and open into the spongy urethra. Their clear, alkaline mucus lubricates this part of the urethra and neutralizes traces of acidic urine. So the glands lie beside one region and empty into the next one downstream.
notes: The prostatic urethra receives the ejaculatory ducts and the prostate's own fluid. Pick it if the question asked where the ejaculatory ducts empty.

The ejaculatory duct is formed by the ductus deferens and the seminal vesicle duct, upstream of the bulbourethral glands. It would be the answer if the question asked where seminal vesicle fluid first joins the sperm.

The membranous urethra is the region the bulbourethral glands sit beside, which is why students pick it, but their ducts open farther down. Choose it if the question asked where the glands are located rather than where they empty.
Correct. Bulbourethral ducts open into the spongy urethra.

questions.q: Which structure contributes the largest share of the fluid in semen?
questions.why: The seminal vesicles produce the largest share of semen, about 60 percent of its volume, an alkaline fluid rich in fructose that gives the sperm energy. The prostate adds a smaller amount of milky fluid, and the bulbourethral glands add only a little mucus. The sperm cells themselves make up a small part of the total volume.
notes: Correct. The seminal vesicles supply most of the fluid in semen.
The bulbourethral glands add a small amount of clear, alkaline mucus. Choose them if the question asked which gland lubricates the urethra.
The prostate adds a milky fluid that helps sperm stay active, but less of it than the seminal vesicles. Pick it if the question asked which gland surrounds the urethra below the bladder.
The seminiferous tubules make the sperm cells, not the fluid. They would be the answer if the question asked where sperm are produced.

questions.q: Which duct carries sperm upward out of the scrotum inside the spermatic cord?
questions.why: The ductus deferens (vas deferens) begins at the tail of the epididymis and carries sperm up out of the scrotum inside the spermatic cord. It passes through the inguinal canal into the pelvis, runs along the back of the bladder, and ends by joining the seminal vesicle duct. Its thick smooth muscle wall pushes sperm along.
notes: The epididymis stores sperm on the back of the testis, just before the ductus deferens begins. Pick it if the question asked where sperm gain the ability to move.
The urethra is the final shared tube for urine and semen, running through the prostate and penis. It would be the answer if the question asked which duct carries sperm to the outside.
Correct. The ductus deferens carries sperm up out of the scrotum in the spermatic cord.
The ejaculatory duct is the short duct deep in the pelvis that forms after the ductus deferens meets the seminal vesicle duct. Choose it if the question asked which duct passes through the prostate.

questions.q: In which structure do sperm gain the ability to swim?
questions.why: Sperm leaving the seminiferous tubules are fully formed but cannot yet swim. They pass into the epididymis, the comma-shaped duct on the back of the testis, where they are stored and gain motility, the ability to move on their own. This maturation step is why the epididymis comes right after the testis on the route.
notes: The seminal vesicles add fructose that fuels swimming, but sperm gain the ability to swim before they meet this fluid. They would be the answer if the question asked which gland makes the largest share of semen.
The ductus deferens moves sperm by contractions of its muscular wall, after they have already matured. Choose it if the question asked which duct carries sperm up through the spermatic cord.
Correct. Sperm gain motility in the epididymis.
The seminiferous tubules produce sperm, but sperm leaving them cannot swim yet. Pick them if the question asked where sperm are made.

questions.q: On their way to the urethra, the ejaculatory ducts pass through which gland?
questions.why: Each ejaculatory duct forms behind the bladder, then runs down through the substance of the prostate to open into the prostatic urethra. The prostate surrounds both the first part of the urethra and the ejaculatory ducts. This is the meeting point where sperm, seminal vesicle fluid, and prostate fluid all come together.
notes: Correct. The ejaculatory ducts pass through the prostate to reach the prostatic urethra.
The testis is in the scrotum, where sperm are made, at the start of the route rather than near the urethra. It would be the answer if the question asked which organ contains the seminiferous tubules.

The seminal vesicles help form the ejaculatory ducts, since their ducts join the ductus deferens, but the ejaculatory ducts do not pass through them. Pick them if the question asked which gland's duct joins the ductus deferens.

The bulbourethral glands are below the prostate and empty into the spongy urethra, downstream of where the ejaculatory ducts end. Choose them if the question asked which glands lie below the prostate.

questions.q: A 68-year-old man has a weak urine stream because a non-cancerous growth of a gland is squeezing his urethra just below the bladder. Which gland is enlarged?
questions.why: The prostate sits just below the bladder and wraps around the prostatic urethra. In benign prostatic hyperplasia, a non-cancerous enlargement common in older men, the growing gland presses inward on the urethra and narrows it. That is how a reproductive gland causes a urinary symptom like a weak stream.
notes: Correct. An enlarged prostate squeezes the urethra just below the bladder.

The bulbourethral glands are pea-sized glands below the prostate that sit beside the urethra but do not encircle it. They would be the answer if the question asked which glands secrete alkaline mucus.
The epididymis is a duct on the back of the testis in the scrotum, nowhere near the bladder or urethra. Pick it if the question asked where sperm are stored and mature.

The seminal vesicles lie on the back of the bladder and do not surround the urethra, so their enlargement would not squeeze it. Choose them if the question asked which glands make the largest share of semen.

questions.q: Which tube carries both urine and semen in a male?
questions.why: The male urethra runs from the bladder through the prostate, the floor of the pelvis, and the penis to the outside. It carries urine from the bladder and semen from the ejaculatory ducts, though never both at the same moment. This shared final stretch is where the urinary and reproductive systems overlap.
notes: Correct. The urethra is the shared tube for urine and semen.

The ejaculatory duct carries only sperm and seminal vesicle fluid, and only for a short distance through the prostate. It would be the answer if the question asked which duct empties into the prostatic urethra.

The ureter carries urine from the kidney to the bladder and never carries semen. Students mix it up with the urethra because the names look alike; pick ureter if the question asked what drains each kidney.
The ductus deferens carries only sperm, from the epididymis up through the spermatic cord. Choose it if the question asked which duct is cut in a vasectomy.

questions.q: A newborn's left testis never moved down into the scrotum and remains in the abdomen. What is this condition called?
questions.why: Cryptorchidism is the failure of one or both testes to descend into the scrotum. The name means hidden testis, because the testis stays out of sight in the abdomen or the inguinal canal. An undescended testis stays at core body temperature, which impairs sperm production and raises the risk of testicular cancer.
notes: An inguinal hernia is a loop of intestine pushing through the weak point at the inguinal canal. Pick it if the question described a bulge of intestine in the groin.
A hydrocele is a collection of serous fluid in the tunica vaginalis around a testis. Choose it if the question described a fluid-filled swelling around a testis that is already in the scrotum.
A varicocele is an abnormal swelling of the veins that drain the testis. It would be the answer if the question described enlarged veins in the scrotum.
Correct. A testis that fails to descend is cryptorchidism.

questions.q: In an inguinal hernia, what pushes through the weak point at the inguinal canal?
questions.why: The inguinal canal is a natural passage through the lower abdominal wall that carries the spermatic cord in males. Because it is an opening, it is a weak point, and in an inguinal hernia a loop of intestine pushes through it, sometimes down toward the scrotum. This shows up as a bulge in the groin.
notes: An undescended testis is cryptorchidism, where a testis stays in the abdomen or groin instead of reaching the scrotum. Pick it if the question asked about a testis that never descended.
Fluid collecting in the tunica vaginalis is a hydrocele. Choose it if the question described a fluid-filled swelling around the testis.
A swollen vein draining the testis is a varicocele. It would be the answer if the question described enlarged veins in the scrotum.
Correct. A loop of intestine pushes through the inguinal canal in an inguinal hernia.

questions.q: On which side of the penis does the corpus spongiosum lie?
questions.why: The corpus spongiosum is the single column of erectile tissue on the ventral side of the penis, below the two corpora cavernosa. It surrounds the spongy urethra, runs the full length of the penis, and expands into the glans at the tip. Its ventral position is why the urethra lies along the underside of the penis.
notes: The dorsal side holds the paired corpora cavernosa. Pick dorsal if the question asked where the two cavernosa run.

The two corpora cavernosa lie side by side, which can look like left and right, but they are both dorsal, and the spongiosum is a single midline column. This option comes from picturing the columns from the wrong angle.
The corpus spongiosum does form the bulb in the root, but it continues through the body all the way to the glans. Limiting it to the root leaves out most of its length.
Correct. The corpus spongiosum is the ventral column.

questions.q: The tunica albuginea divides each testis into a few hundred lobules. Which structures are packed into each lobule?
questions.why: Each lobule of the testis holds tightly coiled seminiferous tubules, the tubes where sperm are produced. The interstitial cells that make testosterone sit in the spaces between these tubules. Coiling long tubules into small lobules fits a great length of sperm-producing tissue into a small organ.
notes: Correct. Seminiferous tubules fill the lobules of the testis.
The pampiniform plexus is a network of veins in the spermatic cord, outside the testis. Choose it if the question asked which veins drain the testis and surround the testicular artery.
Erectile tissue fills the corpora cavernosa and corpus spongiosum of the penis. It would be the answer if the question asked what fills with blood during an erection.
Lactiferous ducts carry milk in the mammary gland, a female structure that is also divided into lobules. Pick them if the question asked which ducts drain the lobes of the breast.

questions.q: During a self-exam, a 25-year-old man finds a firm lump in one testis. If the lump is malignant, which disorder is it?
questions.why: Testicular cancer is a malignant tumor of the testis, usually starting in the sperm-forming cells of the seminiferous tubules. Because the testes hang in the scrotum outside the body, a man can feel them directly, which is why self-exams are taught. A firm lump in the testis itself is the warning sign.
notes: A hydrocele is a collection of serous fluid in the tunica vaginalis around the testis, not a tumor. Pick it if the question described a fluid-filled swelling.

Prostate cancer is a malignant tumor of the prostate, deep in the pelvis below the bladder, so it cannot be felt in the testis. It would be the answer if the question described a malignant growth of the gland around the urethra.
Correct. A malignant tumor of the testis is testicular cancer.
A varicocele is an abnormal swelling of the veins that drain the testis, not a growth in the testis itself. Choose it if the question described enlarged veins in the scrotum.

questions.q: On a sagittal model of the male pelvis, you find a pair of elongated glands pressed against the back of the urinary bladder. What are they?
questions.why: The seminal vesicles are a pair of elongated glands on the posterior surface of the urinary bladder. Each one's duct joins the ampulla of the ductus deferens to form an ejaculatory duct. On a model, look behind the bladder and above the prostate to find them.
notes: Correct. The seminal vesicles are the paired glands on the back of the bladder.

The ureters do reach the back of the bladder, but they are tubes carrying urine from the kidneys, not glands. They would be the answer if the question asked which tubes enter the posterior wall of the bladder.
The prostate is a single gland below the bladder around the urethra, not a pair on its back wall. Choose it if the question asked which gland surrounds the first part of the urethra.
The bulbourethral glands are pea-sized and sit below the prostate, not on the back of the bladder. Pick them if the question asked which glands lie beside the membranous urethra.

questions.q: Which part of the penis is the free, movable shaft?
questions.why: The body, or shaft, is the free, movable portion of the penis between the attached root and the glans at the tip. It contains all three columns of erectile tissue: the two corpora cavernosa and the corpus spongiosum with the spongy urethra inside it.
notes: The glans is the acorn-shaped tip, an expansion of the corpus spongiosum. Choose it if the question asked for the enlarged tip.
The crura are the anchored ends of the corpora cavernosa, found in the root rather than the shaft. They would be the answer if the question asked how the dorsal columns attach to the pelvic bones.
The root is the attached portion anchored in the perineum, containing the bulb and the crura. Pick it if the question asked which part is fixed to the body.
Correct. The body is the free shaft of the penis.

questions.q: Before birth, each testis moves from the abdomen down to the scrotum. Which passage in the abdominal wall does it travel through?
questions.why: The testes form high on the back wall of the abdomen during fetal development and then descend, passing through the inguinal canal in the lower anterior abdominal wall to reach the scrotum. The spermatic cord later runs through this same canal. Because the canal is a natural opening in the wall, it stays a weak point where an inguinal hernia can occur.
notes: The esophageal hiatus is the opening in the diaphragm that the esophagus passes through, the site of a hiatal hernia. Choose it if the question asked where the esophagus crosses from thorax to abdomen.

The obturator canal is a small gap at the top of the obturator foramen of the hip bone that leads into the thigh. It would be the answer if the question asked about a passage from the pelvis into the medial thigh, not into the scrotum.
The umbilical ring is the opening at the navel where the umbilical cord vessels passed, and it is the site of an umbilical hernia. Pick it if the question asked about the opening at the belly button.
Correct. The testes descend through the inguinal canal.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly traces sperm from where they are made, to where they are stored, to the duct that carries them out of the scrotum?
options: Seminiferous tubules, then epididymis, then ductus deferens
Seminiferous tubules, then ductus deferens, then epididymis
Ductus deferens, then epididymis, then seminiferous tubules
Epididymis, then seminiferous tubules, then ductus deferens
questions.why: Sperm are produced in the seminiferous tubules inside the testis. They then move into the epididymis on the back of the testis, where they are stored and gain the ability to move. Finally the ductus deferens carries them up out of the scrotum inside the spermatic cord.
notes: Correct. Production, then storage, then transport out of the scrotum.
This swaps the last two steps. The epididymis sits right on the testis and comes before the ductus deferens, which begins at the tail of the epididymis.
This is the whole route in reverse. It traces the path from the pelvis back toward the testis, which is the direction a student might follow when reading a diagram from the top down.
This puts storage before production. Sperm cannot be stored in the epididymis until the seminiferous tubules have made them, so the tubules always come first.
questions.answerText: Seminiferous tubules, then epididymis, then ductus deferens

questions.q: Sperm have just left the ductus deferens. Which two structures do they pass through next, in order, before leaving the body?
options: The urethra, then the ejaculatory duct
The ejaculatory duct, then the urethra
The rete testis, then the ejaculatory duct
questions.why: The ductus deferens joins the seminal vesicle duct to form the ejaculatory duct, so that is the next stop. The ejaculatory duct then empties into the prostatic urethra, and sperm travel through the prostatic, membranous, and spongy urethra to the outside. The full route is seminiferous tubules, epididymis, ductus deferens, ejaculatory duct, and urethra.
notes: This reverses the two. The ejaculatory duct empties into the urethra, so the urethra must come second.
The epididymis comes before the ductus deferens, not after it. Pick the epididymis if the question asked where sperm go right after leaving the testis.
Correct. Ejaculatory duct first, then the urethra.
The rete testis is the network of channels inside the testis, at the very start of the route. It would be the answer if the question asked where sperm go after the seminiferous tubules.
questions.answerText: The ejaculatory duct, then the urethra

questions.q: Starting at the testis, in what order do sperm reach these three places: the ejaculatory duct, the epididymis, and the inguinal canal?
questions.why: Sperm first enter the epididymis on the back of the testis, inside the scrotum. The ductus deferens then carries them up in the spermatic cord, through the inguinal canal in the abdominal wall, and into the pelvis. Deep in the pelvis, behind the bladder, the ductus deferens joins the seminal vesicle duct to form the ejaculatory duct.
notes: The inguinal canal cannot come first, because sperm are still in the scrotum while in the epididymis. The ductus deferens carries them through the canal only after they leave the epididymis.

The ejaculatory duct is near the end of the route, not the start. This order treats it as if it were in the testis, which is a common mix-up with the small efferent ducts that carry sperm out of the testis.
Correct. Epididymis in the scrotum, then the inguinal canal, then the ejaculatory duct in the pelvis.
The ejaculatory duct lies deep in the pelvis, so sperm must pass through the inguinal canal to reach it. This order skips the trip from the scrotum up into the pelvis.

questions.q: The male reproductive system is sorted into gonads, ducts, accessory glands, and supporting structures. Which two make up the supporting structures?
questions.why: The supporting structures are the scrotum and the penis. The scrotum holds the testes outside the body at a slightly cooler temperature, and the penis delivers sperm into the female reproductive tract and carries the urethra. They neither make sperm nor add fluid, which is why they are grouped separately from the gonads, ducts, and glands.
notes: The testes and their interstitial cells belong to the gonads, which produce sperm and hormones. They would be the answer if the question asked where testosterone is made.
Correct. The scrotum and penis are the supporting structures.
The epididymis and ductus deferens belong to the duct system, which stores and carries sperm. Choose them if the question asked for two parts of the duct system.
The prostate and seminal vesicles are accessory glands that add fluid to semen. Pick them if the question asked for two of the accessory glands.

questions.q: Following the path of sperm downstream, in what order do you pass the places where the three accessory glands empty their fluid?
options: Seminal vesicles, then prostate, then bulbourethral glands
Seminal vesicles, then bulbourethral glands, then prostate
Prostate, then seminal vesicles, then bulbourethral glands
Bulbourethral glands, then prostate, then seminal vesicles
questions.why: The seminal vesicle ducts come first, because they merge with the ductus deferens to form the ejaculatory ducts behind the bladder. The prostate comes next, with its ducts opening into the prostatic urethra just below the bladder. The bulbourethral glands come last, emptying into the spongy urethra below the prostate. This is the order of the openings along the path, not the order in time that each gland releases its fluid.
notes: Correct. The seminal vesicles empty at the ejaculatory ducts, the prostate into the prostatic urethra, and the bulbourethral glands into the spongy urethra.
This swaps the last two. The bulbourethral glands sit below the prostate and open into the spongy urethra, so they come after the prostate, not before it.
This puts the prostate first, but the seminal vesicle fluid joins earlier, at the ejaculatory duct behind the bladder, before the sperm ever reach the prostate.
This is the order reversed. It lists the openings from the tip of the penis back toward the bladder, the opposite of the direction sperm travel.
questions.answerText: Seminal vesicles, then prostate, then bulbourethral glands

questions.q: Name the male gonad, the fibrous capsule that divides it into lobules, and the coiled tubes inside where sperm form.
questions.why: The testis is the male gonad. Its tough white fibrous capsule, the tunica albuginea, sends walls inward that divide it into a few hundred lobules. Each lobule holds tightly coiled seminiferous tubules, where sperm are produced.
notes: The dartos is the smooth muscle layer of the scrotal wall, not a capsule of the testis. Pick it if the question asked which muscle wrinkles the scrotal skin.
Correct. Testis, tunica albuginea, and seminiferous tubules.
The tunica vaginalis is the serous membrane covering the testis, but it does not divide the testis into lobules. Choose it if the question asked for the covering derived from the peritoneum.

The epididymis is a duct on the testis, not the gonad, and the efferent ducts carry sperm out of the testis rather than producing them. This combination describes the exit route, not the sperm factory.

questions.q: What two jobs do the testes perform?
options: Add fructose fluid and nourish sperm
Store sperm and help them mature
questions.why: The testes are the male gonads, and they do two jobs. The seminiferous tubules inside them produce sperm, and the interstitial cells between the tubules secrete hormones, mainly testosterone. Every other male reproductive structure stores, carries, or adds fluid to the sperm the testes make.
notes: Correct. The testes produce sperm and secrete hormones.
Adding a fructose-rich fluid that nourishes sperm is the job of the seminal vesicles. Choose this if the question asked about the glands on the back of the bladder.
Carrying both sperm and urine is the job of the male urethra, the shared final tube. It would be the answer if the question asked what the urethra does.
Storing sperm and helping them mature is the job of the epididymis, the duct on the back of the testis. Pick this if the question asked what the epididymis does.

questions.q: Which list names the structures of the male duct system?
options: Epididymis, ductus deferens, ejaculatory duct, urethra
Seminal vesicles, prostate gland, bulbourethral glands
Epididymis, ductus deferens, ejaculatory duct, ureter
Seminiferous tubules, epididymis, prostate gland, urethra
questions.why: The male duct system is the epididymis, ductus deferens, ejaculatory ducts, and urethra, in that order. These ducts store, mature, and carry sperm from the testis to the outside. The seminiferous tubules make the sperm and the accessory glands add fluid, so neither group is counted as part of the duct system.
notes: Correct. These four ducts make up the male duct system.
These are the three accessory glands, which add fluid to semen rather than carry sperm. Pick this list if the question asked for the accessory glands.
The ureter carries urine from the kidney to the bladder and is part of the urinary system. Replacing the urethra with the ureter is the classic look-alike mix-up.

The seminiferous tubules produce sperm inside the testis, and the prostate is an accessory gland, so this list mixes groups. It would only fit a question asking for structures sperm pass through or near.
questions.answerText: Epididymis, ductus deferens, ejaculatory duct, urethra

questions.q: What does the dartos muscle do?
options: Squeezes urine out of the urinary bladder
Wrinkles the scrotal skin to reduce heat loss
Raises and lowers the testes inside the scrotum
Pushes sperm along the ductus deferens
questions.why: The dartos is a layer of smooth muscle in the scrotal wall. When it contracts, it wrinkles and tightens the scrotal skin, which shrinks the surface area and reduces heat loss from the testes. Together with the cremaster, it helps keep the testes near the temperature sperm production needs.
notes: Squeezing urine out of the bladder is the job of the detrusor, the smooth muscle of the bladder wall. Choose this if the question asked about the detrusor.
Correct. The dartos wrinkles the scrotal skin to reduce heat loss.
Raising and lowering the testes is the job of the cremaster, the skeletal muscle in the spermatic cord. Pick this if the question asked what the cremaster does.
The ductus deferens has its own thick smooth muscle wall that pushes sperm along. This would describe that wall, not a muscle of the scrotum.
questions.answerText: Wrinkles the scrotal skin to reduce heat loss

questions.q: What type of tissue makes up the cremaster muscle?
questions.why: The cremaster is skeletal muscle, the striated type of muscle tissue attached to the trunk and limbs. It runs in the spermatic cord and loops around the testis, raising the testis toward the body in the cold and letting it hang lower when warm. The two scrotal muscles are different tissues: the cremaster is skeletal, and the dartos is smooth.
notes: Cardiac muscle is found only in the wall of the heart. Students who pick it are usually guessing at an involuntary-looking muscle, but the cremaster is not related to the heart.
Correct. The cremaster is skeletal muscle.
Smooth muscle is the tissue of the dartos, the other scrotal muscle, which wrinkles the skin. Pick smooth muscle if the question asked about the dartos.
Dense regular connective tissue forms tendons and ligaments, not a contracting muscle. It would be the answer if the question asked what tissue connects muscle to bone.

questions.q: Along the route of sperm, which structure is the only one that produces sperm rather than storing or carrying them?
questions.why: Only the seminiferous tubules, the coiled tubes inside the testis, make sperm. Every other structure on the route has a different job: the epididymis stores and matures them, and the ductus deferens, ejaculatory duct, and urethra carry them. Sorting the male structures into one producer and several transporters makes the route easier to remember.
notes: The epididymis stores sperm and lets them gain the ability to move, but it does not make them. Pick it if the question asked where sperm mature.
Correct. The seminiferous tubules are the only sperm producers.
The ejaculatory duct is a short duct that carries sperm and seminal vesicle fluid into the prostatic urethra. It would be the answer if the question asked which duct passes through the prostate.
The ductus deferens carries sperm up out of the scrotum through the spermatic cord. Choose it if the question asked which duct is cut in a vasectomy.

questions.q: What is another name for the interstitial cells of the testis?
questions.why: The interstitial cells of the testis are also called Leydig cells. They sit in the spaces between the seminiferous tubules and produce testosterone. Pairing each eponym with its location helps: Leydig cells are between the tubules, and Sertoli cells are inside the tubules.
notes: Correct. Interstitial cells are also called Leydig cells.
Granulosa cells surround the developing oocyte inside an ovarian follicle, a female structure. Choose them if the question asked which cells form the layers of a follicle in the ovary.

Sertoli cells are the sustentacular cells that line the seminiferous tubules, nourish developing sperm, and form the blood-testis barrier. Pick them if the question asked for another name for the sustentacular cells.

Podocytes are cells in the kidney that wrap around the glomerular capillaries and form part of the filtration membrane. They would be the answer if the question asked about the visceral layer of the glomerular capsule.

questions.q: The epididymis belongs to which group of male reproductive structures?
questions.why: The epididymis is the first part of the male duct system, which also includes the ductus deferens, the ejaculatory ducts, and the urethra. It is a coiled duct on the back of the testis where sperm are stored and gain the ability to move. Even though it sits right on the testis, it does not make sperm, so it is a duct and not part of the gonad.
notes: The accessory glands are the seminal vesicles, prostate, and bulbourethral glands, which add fluid to semen. Choose this group if the question asked where the prostate belongs.
The gonads are the testes, which produce sperm and hormones. Pick this group if the question asked where the testes belong.
The supporting structures are the scrotum and the penis. They would be the answer if the question asked which group holds the testes and delivers sperm.
Correct. The epididymis is part of the duct system.

questions.q: In a vasectomy, a surgeon cuts and ties the duct that carries sperm upward from the scrotum in the spermatic cord. Which duct is cut?
questions.why: A vasectomy cuts the ductus deferens, also called the vas deferens, which is where the procedure gets its name. The duct is easy to reach because it runs in the spermatic cord just under the scrotal skin. Once it is cut, sperm cannot travel past the scrotum, but the accessory glands still add their fluid, so semen is still released without sperm.
notes: The epididymis is the coiled duct on the back of the testis where sperm are stored. It sits before the cut, which is why sperm still form and collect there after a vasectomy.

The ejaculatory duct lies deep in the pelvis and passes through the prostate, so it cannot be reached through the scrotum. Pick it if the question asked where the ductus deferens and seminal vesicle duct join.
Correct. A vasectomy cuts the ductus (vas) deferens.
The urethra carries urine as well as semen, so cutting it would block urination. It would be the answer if the question asked which tube is shared by the urinary and reproductive systems.

questions.q: Which list best describes the contents of the spermatic cord?
options: Ductus deferens, blood vessels, nerves, cremaster
Ductus deferens, blood vessels, nerves, dartos
Seminal vesicle ducts, prostate, bulbourethral ducts
Ejaculatory duct, blood vessels, nerves, cremaster
questions.why: The spermatic cord is the bundle that suspends each testis and passes through the inguinal canal. It contains the ductus deferens, blood vessels (the testicular artery and the pampiniform plexus of veins), nerves, lymphatic vessels, and the cremaster muscle. Everything a testis needs to connect to the body travels in this cord.
notes: Correct. The cord holds the ductus deferens, vessels, nerves, and the cremaster.
The dartos is smooth muscle in the wall of the scrotum, not in the spermatic cord. Swapping in the dartos for the cremaster is the common mix-up between the two scrotal muscles.
The seminal vesicles, prostate, and bulbourethral glands are accessory glands in the pelvis, all outside the cord. Pick this list if the question asked which structures add fluid to semen.
The ejaculatory duct lies deep in the pelvis behind the bladder, not in the cord. The duct inside the cord is the ductus deferens, which only later becomes part of the ejaculatory duct.
questions.answerText: Ductus deferens, blood vessels, nerves, cremaster

questions.q: Which part of a sperm cell holds the nucleus with its chromosomes?
questions.why: The head of the sperm holds the nucleus, which carries 23 chromosomes, half the number in a body cell. At fertilization, these chromosomes join the 23 in the oocyte. The head is capped by the acrosome, which holds enzymes that help the sperm get through the coverings of the oocyte.
notes: Correct. The head holds the nucleus and its 23 chromosomes.
The middle piece is packed with mitochondria that power the tail. Pick it if the question asked which part supplies energy for swimming.
The end piece is the thin, tapering last part of the tail. It would be the answer if the question asked for the terminal portion of the tail.
The principal piece is the longest part of the tail and drives most of the swimming motion. Choose it if the question asked for the longest segment of the tail.

questions.q: What is the acrosome of a sperm cell?
options: An enzyme-filled cap over the head
The longest part of the tail
The part of the tail packed with mitochondria
The neck region that holds the centrioles
questions.why: The acrosome is a cap that covers the front of the sperm head, and it is a sac of enzymes. When the sperm reaches the oocyte, these enzymes let it digest a path through the layers that surround the oocyte. It sits on the head because the head carries the nucleus that must get through.
notes: Correct. The acrosome is the enzyme-filled cap over the head.
The longest part of the tail is the principal piece. It would be the answer if the question asked which segment of the tail is longest.
The part of the tail packed with mitochondria is the middle piece. Pick this description if the question asked about the middle piece.
The neck is the short part just behind the head that contains the centrioles. Choose this description if the question asked about the neck.
questions.answerText: An enzyme-filled cap over the head

questions.q: Which structure adds an alkaline fluid rich in fructose to the sperm?
questions.why: The seminal vesicles, the paired glands on the back of the bladder, add an alkaline fluid rich in fructose. Fructose is a sugar the sperm use for energy. This secretion is the largest share of semen, about 60 percent of its volume.
notes: The testes produce the sperm and testosterone, not the fluid that carries the sperm. They would be the answer if the question asked where sperm are made.
The prostate adds a milky fluid that helps sperm stay active, not an alkaline, fructose-rich one. Pick it if the question asked which gland surrounds the prostatic urethra.
The bulbourethral glands add a clear, alkaline mucus that lubricates the urethra, but it is not rich in fructose. Choose them if the question asked which glands neutralize urine in the urethra.
Correct. The seminal vesicles add the alkaline, fructose-rich fluid.

questions.q: What is another name for the bulbourethral glands?
