questions.why: The vagina is the fibromuscular canal that connects the cervix of the uterus to the outside of the body. It receives the penis during intercourse and serves as the birth canal. Its lower opening, the vaginal orifice, opens into the vestibule of the vulva.
notes: The vestibule is the shallow area between the labia minora where the vagina and urethra open. It is a space of the vulva, not a canal. Pick it for the region that holds those two openings.
The urethra is a separate tube that carries urine from the bladder to the outside. It opens into the vestibule just in front of the vagina. Pick it for the tube that drains the bladder.
Correct. The vagina runs from the cervix to the exterior.
The uterine tube runs from beside the ovary to the uterus. It never reaches the outside of the body. Pick it for the tube that carries the oocyte toward the uterus.

questions.q: What are the structures in the ovarian cortex that each hold a developing oocyte called?
questions.why: Ovarian follicles are the structures in the cortex of the ovary, each holding an oocyte at some stage of development. As a follicle matures it enlarges and fills with fluid, and at ovulation the mature follicle releases its oocyte.
notes: Mammary alveoli are the small sacs of glandular tissue in the breast that secrete milk. Pick them for the milk-producing units of the mammary gland.
Seminiferous tubules are the coiled tubules inside the testis where sperm develop. They are the male counterpart of a place where gametes form. Pick them for the testis.
Correct. Each ovarian follicle holds a developing oocyte.
The corpora albicantia (singular, corpus albicans) are white scars in the ovary left after a corpus luteum degenerates. They hold no oocyte. Pick them for the scar tissue in an older ovary.

questions.q: Which small mass of erectile tissue sits at the anterior junction of the labia minora?
questions.why: The clitoris is a small, sensitive mass of erectile tissue where the labia minora meet at the front of the vulva. It fills with blood during arousal and is the female homolog of the penis.
notes: The mons pubis is the cushion of fatty tissue over the pubic symphysis, above and in front of the labia. Pick it for the fatty pad over the pubic bone.
The hymen is a thin fold of mucous membrane that partly closes the vaginal opening. Pick it for the membrane at the vaginal orifice.
The vestibule is the area between the labia minora that holds the vaginal and urethral openings. It lies behind the clitoris. Pick it for the space where those openings are found.
Correct. The clitoris sits where the labia minora meet in front.

questions.q: What are the milk-producing glands of the breast called?
questions.why: The mammary glands are the milk-producing glands of the breasts. They lie over the chest muscles and are built from lobes, lobules, and alveoli, with lactiferous ducts carrying milk to the nipple. They are studied with the female reproductive system because they feed the newborn.
notes: The seminal glands are male accessory glands behind the bladder that add fluid to semen. Pick them for the glands that produce most of the seminal fluid.
The greater vestibular glands are the Bartholin's glands beside the vaginal opening, which secrete lubricating mucus. Pick them for the glands of the vulva.
The bulbourethral glands are small male glands below the prostate that release mucus into the urethra. Pick them for the male homolog of the greater vestibular glands.
Correct. The mammary glands are the milk-producing glands of the breast.

questions.q: What is the circular pigmented area of skin around the nipple called?
questions.why: The areola is the circle of pigmented skin that surrounds the nipple. The nipple itself is the raised projection in the center, where the lactiferous ducts open. Both are on the surface of the breast, while lobules and alveoli are deep inside the gland.
notes: The nipple is the raised projection in the center of the areola where the lactiferous ducts open. Pick it for the opening point of the milk ducts.
A lobule is a subdivision of a mammary lobe, deep inside the breast, that contains the milk-secreting alveoli. Pick it for the subdivision that holds the alveoli.
An alveolus is one of the small sacs of glandular tissue inside a lobule that secretes milk. Pick it for the milk-producing unit of the gland.
Correct. The areola is the pigmented ring of skin around the nipple.

questions.q: After a mature follicle releases its oocyte at ovulation, which structure forms from what remains of that follicle?
questions.why: After ovulation, the ruptured follicle left in the ovary is transformed into the corpus luteum, which means yellow body. It is a temporary structure. If no pregnancy occurs, it later degenerates into a white scar called the corpus albicans.
notes: The germinal epithelium is the layer of low cuboidal cells covering the surface of the ovary. Pick it for the outermost layer of the ovary.
The tunica albuginea is the whitish connective tissue capsule just beneath the germinal epithelium. Pick it for the capsule of the ovary.
Correct. The corpus luteum, the yellow body, forms from the follicle left after ovulation.
The corpus albicans is the white scar that forms later, when the corpus luteum degenerates. It is one step further along. Pick it for what the corpus luteum becomes.

questions.q: Which ligament is the cord that anchors the ovary to the uterus?
questions.why: The ovary is held in place by more than one attachment, and each one connects it to something different. The ovarian ligament is a short cord that ties the ovary medially to the side of the uterus. The suspensory ligament holds it laterally to the pelvic wall, and the mesovarium attaches it to the broad ligament.
notes: Correct. The ovarian ligament anchors the ovary to the uterus.
The uterosacral ligament connects the uterus to the sacrum. Pick it for the posterior attachment of the uterus.
The round ligament runs from the uterus to the labia majora. It does not touch the ovary. Pick it for the uterine ligament that reaches the labia majora.
The suspensory ligament attaches the ovary to the lateral pelvic wall and carries the ovarian vessels. Pick it for the lateral attachment of the ovary.

questions.q: Which ligament attaches the ovary to the lateral pelvic wall and carries the ovarian artery and vein?
questions.why: The suspensory ligament is the fold that holds the ovary to the lateral wall of the pelvis. The ovarian artery and vein travel in this fold to reach the ovary, which is why it is the ligament to look for when you trace the ovarian vessels on a model.
notes: The round ligament runs from the uterus to the labia majora and does not attach to the ovary. Pick it for the uterine ligament that reaches the labia majora.
The uterosacral ligament connects the uterus to the sacrum. Pick it for the posterior anchor of the uterus.
Correct. The suspensory ligament holds the ovary to the pelvic wall and carries its vessels.
The ovarian ligament anchors the ovary medially to the uterus, not to the pelvic wall. Pick it for the cord between the ovary and the uterus.

questions.q: Which part of the uterine tube is the funnel-shaped end that opens into the pelvic cavity near the ovary?
questions.why: Infundibulum means funnel, and that is its shape. It is the open, flared end of the uterine tube that sits beside the ovary and opens into the pelvic cavity. The tube does not attach directly to the ovary, so the infundibulum has to catch the oocyte after it is released.
notes: Correct. The infundibulum is the funnel-shaped end near the ovary.
The fimbriae are the finger-like fringes on the rim of the infundibulum. They are attached to the funnel but are not the funnel itself. Pick them for the projections that sweep the oocyte in.
The isthmus is the narrow, thick-walled segment at the far end of the tube, where it joins the uterus. Pick it for the part of the tube closest to the uterus.
The ampulla is the widest and longest part of the tube, just past the funnel, where fertilization usually happens. Pick it for the usual site of fertilization.

questions.q: In which part of the female tract does fertilization usually occur?
questions.why: The ampulla is the widest and longest part of the uterine tube, between the infundibulum and the isthmus. After the fimbriae sweep the oocyte into the infundibulum, it moves into the ampulla, and this is where sperm usually meet it. The narrow isthmus and the uterus come after the ampulla.
notes: The infundibulum is the funnel-shaped end of the tube that catches the oocyte from the ovary. The oocyte passes through it first, but fertilization usually happens farther along, in the ampulla.
The uterine cavity is the space inside the body of the uterus, past the end of the tube. Fertilization usually happens before the oocyte ever reaches it, out in the ampulla of the tube.
The isthmus is the narrow part of the tube that joins the uterus. The oocyte reaches it after the ampulla, so it is past the usual site of fertilization.
Correct. Fertilization usually happens in the ampulla, the widest part of the uterine tube.

questions.q: Which part of the uterine tube is the narrow, thick-walled segment that joins the uterus?
questions.why: An isthmus is a narrow connecting part, and in the uterine tube it is the short, narrow, thick-walled segment at the medial end where the tube joins the uterus. The oocyte or early embryo passes through it on the way to the uterine cavity.
notes: The fimbriae are the fringe of finger-like projections around the infundibulum. Pick them for the structures that sweep the oocyte into the tube.
Correct. The isthmus is the narrow segment joining the tube to the uterus.
The ampulla is the wide middle segment of the tube where fertilization usually occurs. Pick it if the question asked for the widest part.
The infundibulum is the funnel-shaped end at the opposite end of the tube, near the ovary. Pick it for the open end that catches the oocyte.

questions.q: What are the finger-like projections around the infundibulum that sweep the oocyte into the uterine tube called?
questions.why: The fimbriae are a fringe of finger-like projections around the rim of the infundibulum. They lie close to the ovary and, at ovulation, sweep over its surface to draw the released oocyte into the funnel of the tube.
notes: Villi are finger-like projections of the small intestine lining that increase the surface area for absorption. The shape is similar, which is the trap. Pick villi for the small intestine.
Papillae are small bumps, such as those on the tongue or the dermal papillae of the skin. Pick them for the projections on the surface of the tongue.
Correct. The fimbriae are the fringe of projections on the infundibulum.
Rugae are folds in the wall of a hollow organ, such as the stomach or vagina, that let it stretch. Pick rugae for the folds of the stomach lining.

questions.q: Which region of the uterus is the dome-shaped top, above where the uterine tubes enter?
questions.why: The fundus is the rounded, dome-shaped top of the uterus, above the points where the two uterine tubes enter. Below it is the body, which holds the uterine cavity, and below that is the narrow cervix that projects into the vagina. Use the tube entries as the landmark: anything above them is fundus.
notes: The fornix is the recess of the vagina that surrounds the cervix. It belongs to the vagina, not the uterus. Pick it for the vaginal recess.
Correct. The fundus is the dome-shaped top of the uterus.
The cervix is the narrow inferior portion that opens into the vagina, at the opposite end from the fundus. Pick it for the lowest region of the uterus.
The body is the tapered central portion of the uterus, below the fundus and above the cervix. Pick it for the main middle region.

questions.q: Which layer of the uterine wall is the outer serous layer?
questions.why: The perimetrium is the outermost layer of the uterine wall. It is a serous membrane, part of the visceral peritoneum that covers the organ. Peri means around, so the perimetrium is the layer wrapped around the outside of the uterus.
notes: The parietal peritoneum lines the walls of the abdominopelvic cavity rather than covering an organ. The perimetrium is visceral peritoneum. Pick parietal peritoneum for the layer lining the body wall.
The myometrium is the thick middle layer of smooth muscle. Pick it for the layer that contracts in labor.
Correct. The perimetrium is the outer serous layer of the uterus.
The endometrium is the inner vascular lining that sheds in menstruation. Pick it for the innermost layer.

questions.q: Which layer of the uterine wall is the thick smooth muscle that contracts during labor?
questions.why: The myometrium is the thick middle layer of the uterine wall, made of smooth muscle, and it is thickest in the fundus. It is the layer that contracts during childbirth. Myo means muscle, and that prefix is the fastest way to recognize it.
notes: The perimetrium is the outer serous layer, a thin covering of visceral peritoneum. Pick it for the outermost layer.
The stratum basalis is the deep, permanent part of the endometrium that rebuilds the lining after menstruation. It is not muscle. Pick it for the layer that regenerates the lining.
Correct. The myometrium is the smooth muscle layer that contracts in labor.
The endometrium is the inner vascular lining, not a muscle. Pick it for the layer that sheds in menstruation or where an embryo implants.

questions.q: Which structures of the breast carry milk from the lobes toward the nipple?
questions.why: Milk is made in the alveoli, which sit inside lobules, which are grouped into lobes. Each lobe drains through a lactiferous duct that carries the milk toward the nipple and opens on its surface. Lactiferous means milk-carrying, which matches the job.
notes: The alveoli are the small sacs of glandular tissue where milk is produced. They are the start of the path, not the ducts. Pick them for where milk is made.
The lobules are the subdivisions of each lobe that contain the alveoli. Pick them for the subdivision that holds the milk-secreting sacs.
Correct. The lactiferous ducts carry milk to the nipple.
The suspensory ligaments, or Cooper's ligaments, are connective tissue bands that support the breast. They carry no milk. Pick them for what holds up the breast.

questions.q: In the mammary gland, the milk-secreting alveoli are found within which subdivision?
questions.why: The mammary gland nests in one direction: alveoli sit inside lobules, lobules sit inside lobes, and each lobe drains through a lactiferous duct to the nipple. So the alveoli, the small sacs that secrete milk, are housed within the lobules.
notes: The nipple is the projection where the lactiferous ducts open. It is the end of the path, not where milk is made. Pick it for where milk exits the breast.
Correct. The alveoli are housed in the lobules.
The lactiferous ducts carry milk away from the lobes to the nipple. They are the drainage, not the compartments that hold the alveoli. Pick them for the ducts that carry milk.
The areola is the pigmented ring of skin around the nipple, on the surface of the breast. Pick it for the skin around the nipple.

questions.q: Which part of the vulva is the cushion of fatty tissue over the pubic symphysis?
questions.why: The mons pubis is the rounded cushion of fatty tissue lying over the pubic symphysis, the joint between the two pubic bones. It is the most anterior and superior part of the vulva, and after puberty it is covered with hair.
notes: Correct. The mons pubis is the fatty cushion over the pubic symphysis.
The vestibule is the area between the labia minora that holds the vaginal and urethral openings. Pick it for the space where those openings are found.
The labia majora are the two larger, hair-covered skin folds that extend back from the mons pubis. Pick them for the outer folds of the vulva or for the homolog of the scrotum.
The clitoris is the small mass of erectile tissue where the labia minora meet in front. Pick it for the homolog of the penis.

questions.q: Which two openings are found in the vestibule of the vulva?
questions.why: The vestibule is the area enclosed by the labia minora. Two openings sit in it: the urethral orifice in front and the vaginal orifice behind it. The anus is close by but lies outside the vestibule, in the anal triangle of the perineum.
notes: Correct. The urethra and the vagina both open into the vestibule.
The urethra does open into the vestibule, but the anus does not. The anus lies farther back in the anal triangle of the perineum. Pick this pair for the openings found in the perineum.
The cervix opens into the top of the vagina at the external os, deep inside the body, not into the vestibule. Pick the cervix for where the uterus opens into the vagina.
The vagina opens into the vestibule, but the anus is separate, in the anal triangle behind it. Both openings lie in the perineum, which is where this pair would fit.

questions.q: Which folds of the vulva are the two smaller, hairless skin folds that lie within the labia majora?
questions.why: The vulva has two pairs of skin folds. The labia majora are the larger, outer, hair-covered folds. Inside them are the labia minora, smaller and hairless, which enclose the vestibule and meet in front at the clitoris. Majora means larger and minora means smaller.
notes: The hymen is a thin fold of mucous membrane that partly closes the vaginal opening. It is not a skin fold. Pick it for the membrane at the vaginal orifice.
Correct. The labia minora are the smaller, hairless inner folds.
The labia majora are the larger outer folds, covered with hair, and homologous to the scrotum. Pick them for the outer folds of the vulva.
The mons pubis is a fatty cushion over the pubic symphysis, not a fold. Pick it for the fatty pad over the pubic bone.

questions.q: Which layer of the uterine wall is made of a stratum functionalis and a stratum basalis?
questions.why: The endometrium is the inner mucous lining of the uterus, next to the uterine cavity. It has two layers. The stratum functionalis, next to the cavity, is shed during menstruation, and the stratum basalis, next to the myometrium, stays in place and rebuilds it each cycle.
notes: The perimetrium is the outer serous layer of the uterus, part of the visceral peritoneum. It is a single serous covering with no strata, so it is the answer only for the outermost layer.
Correct. The endometrium is built of a stratum functionalis and a stratum basalis.
The ampulla is not a layer of the uterine wall at all. It is the wide middle part of the uterine tube, where fertilization usually happens.
The myometrium is the thick middle layer of smooth muscle and has no stratum functionalis or basalis. It is the answer for the layer that contracts during childbirth.

questions.q: Endometrial tissue is found growing on the ovaries and the pelvic lining, outside the uterus. What is this disorder called?
questions.why: Endometriosis is the growth of endometrial tissue, the tissue that normally lines the uterus, in places outside the uterus such as the ovaries and the pelvic peritoneum. The name comes from the tissue involved. Fibroids, in contrast, grow in the muscle of the uterine wall.
notes: Correct. Endometriosis is endometrial tissue growing outside the uterus.
Pelvic inflammatory disease is an infection that spreads through the uterus, tubes, and ovaries. Pick it when the question describes an infection rising through the tract.
Uterine fibroids are non-cancerous tumors of the smooth muscle of the myometrium. They grow in the uterine wall, not outside the uterus. Pick fibroids for a muscle tumor of the uterus.
Ovarian cysts are fluid-filled sacs that form on or in an ovary. They are not displaced uterine lining. Pick them for a fluid sac on the ovary.

questions.q: A patient has non-cancerous tumors arising in the smooth muscle of the uterine wall. What is this condition called?
questions.why: Uterine fibroids are benign (non-cancerous) tumors of the smooth muscle of the myometrium, the thick middle layer of the uterine wall. The clue in the question is smooth muscle, which points straight to the myometrium.
notes: Endometriosis is endometrial lining tissue growing outside the uterus. It involves the lining, not the muscle layer. Pick it for uterine lining found on the ovaries or pelvic wall.
Ovarian cysts are fluid-filled sacs on or in an ovary, not muscle tumors of the uterus. Pick them for a fluid sac on the ovary.
Cervical cancer is a malignant tumor of the cervix, the lower part of the uterus. It is cancerous and starts in the cervix, not the muscle wall. Pick it for the cancer screened by a Pap test.
Correct. Uterine fibroids are benign tumors of the myometrium.

questions.q: An infection of the upper reproductive tract spreads through the uterus and tubes and can scar the uterine tubes. What is this disorder called?
questions.why: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) is an infection that climbs from the vagina through the cervix, uterus, and uterine tubes into the pelvic cavity. It can reach the pelvic cavity because the infundibulum is open and does not seal onto the ovary. The infection can leave scarring that narrows a uterine tube. The key word in the question is infection.
notes: Endometriosis is uterine lining tissue growing outside the uterus. It can also scar pelvic organs, but it is not an infection. Pick it for endometrial tissue on the ovaries or pelvic wall.
Cervical cancer is a malignant tumor of the cervix. It is not an infection that spreads up the tract. Pick it for the cancer screened by a Pap test.
Correct. Pelvic inflammatory disease is an infection that spreads up the tract and can scar the tubes.
Ovarian cysts are fluid-filled sacs on or in an ovary, not a spreading infection. Pick them for a fluid sac on the ovary.

questions.q: A Pap test screens for cancer by sampling cells from which structure?
questions.why: A Pap test collects cells from the cervix, the narrow lower part of the uterus that projects into the vagina. Because the cervix can be reached through the vagina, its cells can be sampled in a routine exam and checked for changes that can lead to cervical cancer.
notes: Correct. The Pap test samples cells from the cervix to screen for cervical cancer.
The labia minora are skin folds of the vulva. They are external, not the site of a Pap sample. Pick them for the inner folds that enclose the vestibule.
The fundus is the dome-shaped top of the uterus, far from the vagina. Pick it for the superior region of the uterus.
The ovary sits deep in the pelvis beside the uterus and cannot be reached through the vagina for a cell sample. Pick it for a question about ovarian cysts.

questions.q: What are the small sacs of glandular tissue inside the lobules that secrete milk called?
questions.why: The alveoli are the smallest units of the mammary gland, tiny sacs of glandular tissue that secrete milk. They cluster inside the lobules, the lobules group into lobes, and the lobes drain through lactiferous ducts to the nipple.
notes: The lobes are the largest compartments of the mammary gland, 15 to 20 of them, each divided into lobules. They are too large to be the small secreting sacs.
The lactiferous ducts carry milk from the lobes to the nipple. They transport milk rather than make it.
Correct. The alveoli are the milk-secreting sacs inside the lobules.
The lobules are the subdivisions of a lobe that contain the alveoli. They hold the sacs but are not the sacs themselves.

questions.q: Which pigmented projection on the breast is where the lactiferous ducts open?
questions.why: The nipple is the raised, pigmented projection at the center of the breast. The lactiferous ducts converge on it and open on its surface, so it is the exit point for milk. The areola is the ring of pigmented skin around it.
notes: A lobule is a deep subdivision of a lobe that contains the alveoli. Pick it for the subdivision holding the milk-secreting sacs.
The areola is the circular pigmented skin around the nipple. It surrounds the opening point but is not where the ducts open. Pick it for the ring of skin around the nipple.
Correct. The lactiferous ducts open on the nipple.
An alveolus is a milk-secreting sac deep inside a lobule. It is the start of the milk path, not the exit. Pick it for where milk is produced.

questions.q: What is the area enclosed by the labia minora, into which the vagina opens, called?
questions.why: The vestibule is the space between the labia minora. It holds the vaginal orifice and, in front of it, the external urethral orifice. The ducts of the greater vestibular glands also open into the vestibule, which is how those glands got their name.
notes: Correct. The vestibule is the area between the labia minora.
The mons pubis is the fatty cushion over the pubic symphysis, above and in front of the labia. Pick it for the fatty pad over the pubic bone.
The fornix is the recess at the top of the vagina around the cervix. It is deep inside the body, not between the labia. Pick it for the vaginal recess around the cervix.

The perineum is the larger diamond-shaped region that holds all the external genitalia and the anus. The vestibule is a small part within it. Pick the perineum for the whole region from the pubic symphysis to the coccyx.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly traces the oocyte from ovulation until it enters the uterine tube?
questions.why: At ovulation the mature follicle releases the oocyte from the surface of the ovary. The tube is not attached to the ovary, so the fimbriae sweep over the ovary and draw the oocyte toward the tube. The oocyte then enters the funnel-shaped infundibulum, the opening of the uterine tube.
notes: This order has the oocyte enter the funnel before the fimbriae act. The fimbriae are the fringes that guide it in, so they come before the infundibulum.
The oocyte starts in the ovary, so the ovary must be first. The fimbriae cannot act on an oocyte that has not been released yet.
This order starts in the tube, which reverses the direction of travel. The oocyte begins in the ovary and moves into the tube.
Correct. Released from the ovary, swept by the fimbriae, then into the infundibulum.

questions.q: After the oocyte enters the infundibulum, which two regions does it pass through, in order, before reaching the uterine cavity?
questions.why: The oocyte follows one route down the uterine tube. From the funnel-shaped infundibulum it moves into the ampulla, the widest part, where sperm may fertilize it. It then passes through the isthmus, the narrow part that joins the uterus, and reaches the uterine cavity.
notes: Correct. Ampulla first, then isthmus, then the uterine cavity.
The fimbriae are on the rim of the infundibulum and act before the oocyte enters the tube. They are behind it at this point, not ahead.
The ampulla is right, but the cervix is not part of the tube. It is the lowest part of the uterus, below the uterine cavity, so the oocyte would not pass through it on the way in.
This reverses the two regions. The wide ampulla comes first after the funnel, and the narrow isthmus comes last, next to the uterus.

questions.q: Which order lists the layers of the uterine wall from the outer surface to the inner lining?
questions.why: From outside to inside, the uterine wall has the perimetrium (the outer serous layer), the myometrium (the thick smooth muscle in the middle), and the endometrium (the inner vascular lining). The prefixes help: peri means around, myo means muscle, and endo means within.
notes: Correct. Perimetrium outside, myometrium in the middle, endometrium inside.
This puts the muscle layer on the outside. The perimetrium is the outermost covering, so the myometrium cannot come first.
This swaps the inner two layers. The lining faces the cavity, so the endometrium is innermost, with the myometrium between it and the perimetrium.
This is the correct sequence run backward, from the lining out to the surface. It would be right if the question asked for the order from inside to outside.

questions.q: Which order lists the regions of the uterus from the top down to the opening into the vagina?
questions.why: The uterus is shaped like an upside-down pear. The fundus is the dome-shaped top above the entries of the uterine tubes, the body is the tapered central portion, and the cervix is the narrow lowest portion that opens into the vagina.
notes: This is the correct order run from the bottom up. It would be right if the question asked for the order from the vagina upward.
This places the body above the fundus. The fundus is the topmost region, above the tube entries, so it comes first.
This puts the cervix in the middle. The cervix is the narrow neck at the bottom that opens into the vagina, so it comes last.
Correct. Fundus at the top, body in the middle, cervix at the bottom.

questions.q: Which order lists the parts of the mammary gland from the largest division down to the milk-secreting sac?
questions.why: The mammary gland is nested. Each breast has 15 to 20 lobes, each lobe is divided into smaller lobules, and each lobule holds clusters of alveoli, the small sacs that secrete milk. Going from largest to smallest runs lobes, lobules, alveoli.
notes: This places the alveoli above the lobules. The alveoli sit inside the lobules, so they are the smallest unit and come last.
Correct. Lobes contain lobules, and lobules contain alveoli.
This puts lobules before lobes, but lobules are subdivisions of a lobe, so the lobe is larger and comes first.
This is the correct order run from smallest to largest. It would be right if the question asked for the order from the milk sac outward.

questions.q: Name, in order, the female gonad, the structure left in it after a follicle releases its oocyte, and the funnel-shaped tube end that receives that oocyte.
options: The ovary, the corpus luteum, and the infundibulum
The uterus, the corpus luteum, and the infundibulum
The ovary, the corpus luteum, and the ampulla
The ovary, the corpus albicans, and the infundibulum
questions.why: The ovary is the female gonad. After ovulation, the follicle that released the oocyte becomes the corpus luteum, the yellow body. The oocyte is swept by the fimbriae into the infundibulum, the funnel-shaped end of the uterine tube. Each choice changes one of these three pieces, so check each piece in turn.
notes: Correct. Ovary, corpus luteum, and infundibulum.
The uterus is not a gonad. It is the organ where an embryo implants. The other two pieces are right, but the gonad has to be the ovary.
The ampulla is the wide middle part of the tube where fertilization usually occurs. The oocyte reaches it after the infundibulum, so it is one step too far along.
The corpus albicans is the white scar that forms later, when the corpus luteum degenerates. It is the structure one step after the corpus luteum, so pick it for what the corpus luteum becomes.
questions.answerText: The ovary, the corpus luteum, and the infundibulum

questions.q: Which region of the ovary contains the ovarian follicles?
questions.why: The ovarian cortex is the region just beneath the tunica albuginea, and it holds the follicles at their different stages of development. Deeper still is the medulla, which carries the blood vessels and nerves. When you look for follicles on a slide, look in the outer cortex, not the center.
notes: The ovarian medulla is the deep central region of looser connective tissue that carries blood vessels and nerves. Pick it for where the ovary's vessels run.
Correct. The follicles sit in the ovarian cortex.
The germinal epithelium is the layer of low cuboidal cells covering the surface of the ovary. Despite its name, it does not hold the follicles. Pick it for the surface layer.
The tunica albuginea is the whitish capsule of dense connective tissue just beneath the germinal epithelium. Pick it for the capsule of the ovary.

questions.q: If no pregnancy occurs, the corpus luteum degenerates into a white scar in the ovary. What is that scar called?
questions.why: The corpus luteum, or yellow body, is temporary. If no pregnancy occurs, it breaks down and is replaced by a white scar of connective tissue called the corpus albicans, meaning white body. Both are found in the ovary on a slide and are named for their color.
notes: The mature follicle is the large, fluid-filled follicle that releases the oocyte at ovulation. It comes before the corpus luteum, not after. Pick it for the follicle ready to ovulate.
Correct. The corpus luteum degenerates into the corpus albicans.
The tunica albuginea is also white, and its name shares the root alb for white, but it is the capsule just beneath the ovary's surface, not a scar. Pick it for the capsule of the ovary.
The ovarian medulla is the deep central region that carries vessels and nerves. Pick it for the innermost region of the ovary.

questions.q: Which description fits the fimbriae?
options: Small sacs in the breast that secrete milk
Recesses of the vagina surrounding the cervix
Folds of peritoneum that drape over the uterus
Finger-like projections that sweep the oocyte in
questions.why: The fimbriae are a fringe of finger-like projections around the rim of the infundibulum, the funnel-shaped end of the uterine tube. Because the tube is not attached to the ovary, the fimbriae sweep over its surface at ovulation and draw the released oocyte into the tube.
notes: This describes the alveoli of the mammary gland. Pick this description when the question names the alveoli.
This describes the fornix of the vagina. Pick this description when the question names the fornix.
This describes the broad ligament, the peritoneal fold over the uterus and tubes. Pick this description when the question names the broad ligament.
Correct. The fimbriae are the finger-like projections that sweep the oocyte into the tube.
questions.answerText: Finger-like projections that sweep the oocyte in

questions.q: Which set names the three regions of the uterus?
questions.why: The uterus has three regions: the fundus, the rounded top above the entry of the uterine tubes; the body, the main central part that holds the uterine cavity; and the cervix, the narrow lower part that projects into the vagina. Other organs reuse some of these words, since the stomach also has a fundus and a body and the pancreas has a head, body, and tail. Only the uterus has a cervix.
notes: The cortex, medulla, and pelvis are regions of the kidney. Pick this set for a question about kidney regions.
Correct. Fundus, body, and cervix are the regions of the uterus.
The head, body, and tail are the regions of the pancreas. Pick this set for a question about the pancreas.
The cardia, fundus, and pylorus are regions of the stomach. The shared word fundus is the trap. Pick this set for a question about the stomach.

questions.q: Which layer of the uterine wall is partly shed during menstruation?
questions.why: The endometrium is the inner mucous lining of the uterus, next to the uterine cavity. It has two layers. The stratum functionalis, next to the cavity, is the part shed during menstruation, and the deeper stratum basalis stays in place and rebuilds it each cycle.
notes: The tunica albuginea is the capsule of the ovary, not a layer of the uterus. Pick it for the whitish capsule beneath the ovary's surface.
The perimetrium is the outer serous covering of the uterus. It is not shed. Pick it for the outermost layer.
Correct. The endometrium is the layer that sheds in menstruation.
The myometrium is the smooth muscle layer. It stays intact each cycle. Pick it for the layer that contracts during labor.

questions.q: Which female external structure is homologous to the penis?
questions.why: Homologous structures develop from the same embryonic tissue. The clitoris and the penis both form from the same embryonic swelling and both contain erectile tissue that fills with blood during arousal. That is why the clitoris is the female homolog of the penis.
notes: The vestibule is the area between the labia minora that holds the urethral and vaginal openings. Pick it for that space.
Correct. The clitoris is the homolog of the penis.
The mons pubis is the fatty cushion over the pubic symphysis. Pick it for the fatty pad at the front of the vulva.
The labia majora are homologous to the scrotum, not the penis. Pick them for the female homolog of the scrotum.

questions.q: What is another name for the greater vestibular glands?
questions.why: The greater vestibular glands are also called Bartholin's glands. They sit on each side of the vaginal opening and secrete lubricating mucus into the vestibule. Eponyms are easy to mix up, so link Bartholin with the vagina and Cowper with the male urethra.
notes: Montgomery's glands are small glands in the areola of the breast. Pick them for the bumps on the areola around the nipple.
Correct. Bartholin's glands is another name for the greater vestibular glands.
Skene's glands are the paraurethral glands that open near the urethral orifice, not beside the vaginal opening. Pick them if the question asked about the small glands beside the female urethra.
Cowper's glands are the male bulbourethral glands, the homologs of the greater vestibular glands. Pick them for the small glands below the male prostate.

questions.q: The mammary glands are modified versions of which kind of gland?
questions.why: The mammary glands develop from the skin and are modified sweat glands. Like sweat glands, they are exocrine glands that release a product through ducts onto the skin surface, in this case milk through the lactiferous ducts at the nipple.
notes: Correct. The mammary glands are modified sweat glands.

Endocrine glands release hormones into the blood with no ducts. The mammary glands release milk through ducts, so they are exocrine. Pick endocrine glands for organs like the thyroid or adrenal glands.
Sebaceous glands are oil glands of the skin that usually empty into hair follicles. They are a different skin gland. Pick them for a question about where sebum comes from.
Salivary glands are digestive glands around the mouth that secrete saliva. Pick them for the parotid, submandibular, or sublingual glands.

questions.q: The mature follicle releases the oocyte at ovulation. Which structures catch it first?
questions.why: The uterine tube is not attached to the ovary, so the released oocyte has to be caught. The fimbriae sweep over the ovary and draw the oocyte into the infundibulum, the funnel-shaped opening of the tube. Only after that does it move on to the ampulla and the isthmus.
notes: The isthmus and uterine cavity are at the far end of the route, near and inside the uterus. They would be the last stops for an oocyte or early embryo.
Correct. The fimbriae sweep the oocyte into the infundibulum.
The fundus and uterine cavity are parts of the uterus. The oocyte reaches the uterine cavity only at the end of its trip down the tube.
The ampulla and isthmus come later on the route. The oocyte reaches the ampulla only after it has entered through the infundibulum.

questions.q: Which uterine ligament runs from the uterus to the labia majora?
questions.why: The round ligaments are paired fibrous cords that leave the uterus just below the uterine tubes, travel forward through the inguinal canal, and end in the labia majora. Each uterine ligament is easiest to learn by naming what it connects the uterus to.
notes: The uterosacral ligament connects the uterus to the sacrum. Pick it for the posterior anchor of the uterus.
The cardinal ligament runs from the lateral pelvic wall to the cervix and vagina. Pick it for the ligament that anchors the cervix to the side walls.
The broad ligament is the fold of peritoneum that attaches the uterus to the lateral pelvic walls. Pick it for the peritoneal sheet over the uterus and tubes.
Correct. The round ligament runs from the uterus to the labia majora.

questions.q: At which opening does the cervical canal open into the vagina?
questions.why: The cervical canal runs through the cervix and has two openings. The lower one, the external os, opens into the vagina. The upper one, the internal os, opens into the uterine cavity. External means toward the outside, so the external os is the end that faces the vagina.
notes: The internal os is the upper opening of the cervical canal, into the uterine cavity. Pick it if the question asked where the canal opens into the uterus.
The fornix is the vaginal recess that surrounds the cervix, not an opening of the canal. Pick it for the gutter around the cervix.
Correct. The external os opens into the vagina.
The vaginal orifice is where the vagina opens into the vestibule, at the bottom of the tract. Pick it for the external opening of the vagina.

questions.q: Which female external structure is homologous to the male scrotum?
questions.why: The labia majora and the scrotum develop from the same paired swellings in the embryo. In males these swellings fuse to form the scrotum. In females they stay separate as the two larger, hair-covered skin folds of the vulva.
notes: The mons pubis is the fatty cushion over the pubic symphysis. Pick it for the fatty pad at the front of the vulva.
The clitoris is homologous to the penis, not the scrotum. Pick it for the female homolog of the penis.
The vestibule is the area between the labia minora that holds the urethral and vaginal openings. Pick it for that space.
Correct. The labia majora are the homolog of the scrotum.

questions.q: An oocyte travels through the ampulla. Which part of the uterine tube does it pass through next on the way to the uterus?
questions.why: The route through the tube runs infundibulum, ampulla, isthmus, and then the uterine cavity. After the wide ampulla, the oocyte or early embryo passes through the isthmus, the narrow segment that joins the tube to the uterus.
notes: The uterine cavity is the destination, but it comes after the isthmus, not right after the ampulla. It is one step too far.
The fimbriae are on the rim of the infundibulum at the very start of the route. Pick them for what sweeps the oocyte into the tube.
Correct. The isthmus comes right after the ampulla.
The infundibulum is the funnel at the start of the tube, which the oocyte has already passed. Pick it for the structure that receives the oocyte from the ovary.

questions.q: Which thin fold of mucous membrane partly closes the vaginal opening?
questions.why: The hymen is a thin fold of mucous membrane at the vaginal orifice that partly closes the opening. It varies widely in shape and thickness from person to person. It sits at the bottom of the vagina, where the vagina opens into the vestibule.
notes: The labia minora are hairless skin folds that enclose the vestibule. They lie outside the vaginal opening and do not close it. Pick them for the inner folds of the vulva.
Correct. The hymen partly closes the vaginal opening.
The fornix is the recess at the top of the vagina around the cervix, at the opposite end from the opening. Pick it for the vaginal recess around the cervix.
The vestibule is the area between the labia minora into which the vagina opens. It is a space, not a fold of membrane. Pick it for the region holding the vaginal and urethral openings.

questions.q: The broad ligament attaches to the ovary by which portion?
questions.why: The broad ligament is the fold of peritoneum draped over the uterus and tubes. The part of it that attaches to the ovary is called the mesovarium. The prefix meso- is used for peritoneal folds that suspend an organ, just as the mesentery suspends the small intestine.
notes: The suspensory ligament attaches the ovary to the lateral pelvic wall and carries the ovarian vessels. Pick it for the lateral attachment of the ovary.
The ovarian ligament is a separate cord that anchors the ovary to the uterus. Pick it for the ovary-to-uterus attachment.
Correct. The mesovarium is the part of the broad ligament that attaches to the ovary.
The round ligament runs from the uterus to the labia majora and does not attach to the ovary. Pick it for the cord that reaches the labia majora.

questions.q: In pelvic inflammatory disease, infection can climb from the vagina through the uterus and tubes and reach the pelvic cavity. Which structure provides that open route into the cavity?
options: The isthmus of the uterine tube
The external os of the cervix
questions.why: The infundibulum opens into the pelvic cavity near the ovary instead of sealing onto it. That opening is how the fimbriae catch the oocyte, but it also leaves an open path from the outside into the pelvic cavity: vagina, cervix, uterus, uterine tube, and out through the infundibulum. An infection can climb that same route.
notes: The isthmus is the narrow part of the tube next to the uterus. Infection passes through it, but it connects the ampulla to the uterus and does not open into the pelvic cavity.
The external os opens from the cervical canal into the vagina. It is part of the route, but it connects two parts of the tract and does not open into the pelvic cavity.
Correct. The open infundibulum connects the tract to the pelvic cavity.
The fornix is the recess of the vagina that rings the cervix. It is a dead end inside the vagina and does not open into the pelvic cavity.

questions.q: Which pairing of uterine layer and disorder is correct?
questions.why: Uterine fibroids are non-cancerous tumors of smooth muscle, and the smooth muscle of the uterus is the myometrium. Endometriosis, despite sounding similar, involves the endometrium, the lining, growing outside the uterus. Matching each disorder to the tissue it starts in sorts these out.
notes: The endometrium is the lining, not muscle, so it is not where fibroids grow. The endometrium pairs with endometriosis, where lining tissue grows outside the uterus.
The myometrium is the muscle layer, but endometriosis involves lining tissue. This pairing mixes the layer of one disorder with the name of the other.
Correct. Fibroids are smooth muscle tumors of the myometrium.
The perimetrium is the thin outer serous layer, not muscle. Fibroids start in the myometrium beneath it. Pick the perimetrium for the outer covering of the uterus.

questions.q: The endometrium has two layers. Which one stays in place each cycle and rebuilds the lining after menstruation?
questions.why: The endometrium is built in two layers so that it can renew itself. The superficial stratum functionalis thickens each cycle and is shed in menstruation. The deeper stratum basalis is permanent and is never shed, so it regenerates a new functionalis each cycle.
notes: Correct. The stratum basalis is permanent and rebuilds the lining.
The perimetrium is the outer serous layer of the uterus. Pick it for the outermost covering.
The stratum functionalis is the layer that is shed in menstruation, so it cannot be the one that stays behind. Pick it for the part of the lining lost during menstruation.
The myometrium is the smooth muscle layer outside the endometrium. It is not part of the lining. Pick it for the layer that contracts in labor.

questions.q: Unlike a sperm, the oocyte cannot move on its own. What moves it along the uterine tube toward the uterus?
options: Cilia and smooth muscle of the tube wall
Its own flagellum, as a sperm uses
questions.why: The lining of the uterine tube has ciliated cells, and the cilia beat toward the uterus. A layer of smooth muscle in the tube wall also squeezes in waves. Together they move the oocyte toward the uterus over a few days, because the oocyte has no tail of its own.
notes: The myometrium is the muscle of the uterine wall, not of the tube, so it cannot move the oocyte along the tube. It is the layer that contracts during childbirth.
The rupture of the follicle releases the oocyte from the ovary into the pelvic cavity, but it does not push the oocyte down the tube.
Correct. Beating cilia and waves of smooth muscle in the tube wall carry the oocyte toward the uterus.
Only sperm have a flagellum. The oocyte has no tail, so it cannot swim. This choice comes from assuming both gametes move the same way.
questions.answerText: Cilia and smooth muscle of the tube wall

questions.q: Which kind of tissue makes up the myometrium, the thick middle layer of the uterine wall?
questions.why: The myometrium is the thick middle layer of the uterine wall, and it is made of smooth muscle. It is thickest in the fundus, and it is the layer that contracts during childbirth. Like the smooth muscle in other hollow organs, it contracts without conscious control.
notes: Cardiac muscle is the branched, striated muscle joined by intercalated discs in the wall of the heart. It is not in the uterine wall.
Dense regular connective tissue forms tendons and ligaments. It resists pulling but cannot contract, so it cannot be a muscle layer.
Skeletal muscle is the voluntary, striated muscle attached to bones. It is not found in the uterine wall.
Correct. The myometrium is a thick layer of smooth muscle.

questions.q: After ovulation, which glandular body forms in the ovary from the granulosa and theca cells left behind?
questions.why: At ovulation the mature follicle ruptures and releases the secondary oocyte. The granulosa and theca cells left behind become the corpus luteum, the yellow body, a large glandular body. If no pregnancy occurs, it later breaks down into the corpus albicans, a pale scar.
notes: The corpus albicans is the white scar that forms later, when the corpus luteum breaks down. It is one step too far along.
Correct. The cells left behind after ovulation form the corpus luteum.
The ovarian medulla is the central core of loose connective tissue with the blood vessels and nerves. It is a region of the ovary, not a body that forms after ovulation.
The germinal epithelium is the single layer of cuboidal cells covering the ovary. It is the surface layer and does not form from the ruptured follicle.

questions.q: Which paired ligaments run from the lateral pelvic wall to the cervix and vagina?
questions.why: The cardinal ligaments, also called the transverse cervical ligaments, run from the cervix and upper vagina out to the lateral pelvic walls. They are the main support that keeps the uterus from sliding down. The other uterine ligaments are named for where they go: the round ligaments to the labia majora and the uterosacral ligaments to the sacrum.
notes: Correct. The cardinal ligaments anchor the cervix and vagina to the lateral pelvic walls.
The round ligaments run from the uterus forward to the labia majora. Pick them for the uterine ligament that reaches the labia majora.
The uterosacral ligaments run from the uterus back to the sacrum. Pick them for the posterior anchor of the uterus.
The ovarian ligaments tie each ovary to the uterus. Pick them for the attachment between the ovary and the uterus.

questions.q: What is the whitish capsule of dense connective tissue just beneath the surface epithelium of the ovary called?
questions.why: The tunica albuginea is a tough, whitish capsule of dense connective tissue that lies just under the germinal epithelium and wraps the ovary. Albuginea refers to its white color. The testis has a capsule with the same name, which helps you remember that both gonads are wrapped this way.
notes: The ovarian cortex lies beneath the capsule and contains the follicles. Pick it for the region that holds the follicles.
The perimetrium is the outer serous layer of the uterus, not the ovary. Pick it for the outermost layer of the uterine wall.
The corpus albicans is also white, but it is a scar inside the ovary left when a corpus luteum breaks down. Pick it for what remains of a corpus luteum.
Correct. The tunica albuginea is the whitish capsule of the ovary.

questions.q: Which region of the ovary is the deep core of looser connective tissue that carries blood vessels and nerves?
questions.why: The ovarian medulla is the central region of the ovary. It is made of looser connective tissue and holds the blood vessels and nerves that serve the organ. Medulla means the middle or inner part, the same word used for the inner region of the kidney and the adrenal gland.
notes: The ovarian cortex is the outer region that holds the follicles. Pick it if the question asked where the follicles are found.
Correct. The medulla is the central core with the vessels and nerves.
The tunica albuginea is the whitish capsule just beneath the surface. Pick it for the capsule of the ovary.
The germinal epithelium is the layer of low cuboidal cells on the outer surface. Pick it for the outermost layer.

questions.q: On an ovary slide, which structure is the large, fluid-filled follicle ready to release its oocyte at ovulation?
questions.why: As a follicle develops in the ovarian cortex it grows and fills with fluid. The largest stage, the mature follicle, bulges at the surface of the ovary and releases its oocyte at ovulation. What is left of it afterward becomes the corpus luteum.
notes: The germinal epithelium is the thin layer of cuboidal cells covering the ovary, not a follicle. Pick it for the surface layer of the ovary.
The corpus albicans is the white scar left when the corpus luteum breaks down. Pick it for the scar tissue in the ovary.
The corpus luteum forms from the follicle after ovulation, so it no longer holds an oocyte. Pick it for the structure left behind after the oocyte is released.
Correct. The mature follicle is the large, fluid-filled follicle about to ovulate.

questions.q: Which layer of the endometrium is shed during menstruation?
questions.why: The endometrium has two layers. The stratum functionalis, next to the uterine cavity, is the part shed during menstruation. The stratum basalis, next to the myometrium, stays in place and rebuilds the functionalis each cycle.
notes: The perimetrium is the outer serous covering of the uterus. Pick it for the outermost layer of the uterine wall.
Correct. The stratum functionalis is shed in menstruation.
The myometrium is the smooth muscle layer outside the endometrium. It is not shed. Pick it for the layer that contracts during labor.
The stratum basalis is the permanent deep layer that stays behind and rebuilds the lining. Pick it for the layer that regenerates the endometrium.

questions.q: The perineum is divided into two triangles. What is the anterior triangle, which holds the external genitalia, called?
questions.why: A line drawn between the two ischial tuberosities splits the diamond-shaped perineum into two triangles. The anterior one is the urogenital triangle, which holds the external genitalia and the urethral opening. The posterior one is the anal triangle, which holds the anus.
notes: The vestibule is a small space between the labia minora that lies within the urogenital triangle. Pick it for the area that holds the vaginal and urethral openings.
The anal triangle is the posterior half of the perineum and holds the anus. Pick it for the back triangle.
The femoral triangle is in the upper anterior thigh and holds the femoral vessels and nerve. It is not part of the perineum. Pick it for a lower limb question.
Correct. The urogenital triangle is the anterior part of the perineum.

questions.q: The breast lies on the anterior chest wall. Which muscle does most of it rest on?
questions.why: Each breast lies in the subcutaneous tissue in front of the pectoralis major, the large fan-shaped muscle of the anterior chest. The suspensory ligaments run from the skin through the breast to the fascia over this muscle and support the breast.
notes: Correct. Most of the breast rests on the pectoralis major.
The trapezius is a large muscle of the upper back and neck, so it lies on the back of the body, not under the breast.
The latissimus dorsi is the broad muscle of the lower back that wraps toward the armpit. It is on the back, not under the breast on the anterior chest.
The deltoid caps the shoulder and covers the shoulder joint. It sits lateral to the chest, not under the breast.

questions.q: What is the interior space inside the body of the uterus called?
questions.why: The uterine cavity is the space inside the body of the uterus, lined by the endometrium. The uterine tubes open into it at the top, and below it narrows into the cervical canal at the internal os.
notes: The vestibule is the area between the labia minora where the vagina and urethra open. Pick it for that external space.
The vaginal fornix is the recess of the vagina around the cervix. Pick it for the vaginal recess, not the inside of the uterus.
The cervical canal is the passage through the cervix, below the uterine cavity. Pick it for the interior of the cervix.
Correct. The uterine cavity is the space inside the body of the uterus.

questions.q: In the female pelvis, the uterus lies between which two organs?
options: The pubic symphysis in front and the bladder behind
The bladder in front and the kidneys behind
The rectum in front and the bladder behind
The bladder in front and the rectum behind
questions.why: The uterus is a thick-walled, pear-shaped organ in the pelvic cavity. The urinary bladder sits anterior to it and the rectum sits posterior to it. The peritoneum dips between them to form the vesicouterine pouch in front and the rectouterine pouch behind.
notes: The bladder lies directly behind the pubic symphysis, so the bladder, not the uterus, is the next organ back from the pubic bone. The uterus lies behind the bladder.
The kidneys are high in the posterior abdomen, well above the pelvis. The organ behind the uterus is the rectum. Pick the kidneys for a question about retroperitoneal organs of the abdomen.
This is the right pair of organs in the wrong order. The bladder is anterior, just behind the pubic symphysis, and the rectum is posterior, in front of the sacrum.
Correct. Bladder in front, rectum behind.
questions.answerText: The bladder in front and the rectum behind

questions.q: Within the vestibule, how is the urethral orifice positioned relative to the vaginal orifice?
questions.why: Both the urethra and the vagina open into the vestibule, the area between the labia minora. The urethral orifice lies in front, between the clitoris and the vaginal orifice, and the vaginal orifice lies behind it. The anus is farther back still, outside the vestibule.
notes: The greater vestibular glands open beside the vaginal orifice, on each side. Pick lateral if the question asked where those glands open.
Posterior to the vaginal orifice lies the rest of the perineum and then the anus, not the urethra. This choice reverses the two openings.
Correct. The urethral orifice is anterior to the vaginal orifice.
The urethra has its own separate opening and does not empty into the vagina. This choice comes from assuming the two tubes share an exit.

questions.q: What type of epithelium forms the germinal epithelium on the surface of the ovary?
questions.why: The germinal epithelium is a single layer of cuboidal cells covering the ovary, so it is a simple cuboidal epithelium. Despite its name, it does not make oocytes; the oocytes develop in follicles in the cortex beneath it. Under it lies the tunica albuginea, the dense connective tissue capsule.
notes: Stratified squamous epithelium has many layers with flat cells on top. It lines the vagina and covers the skin. Pick it for a surface that takes friction.
Transitional epithelium stretches and lines the urinary bladder and ureters. Pick it for an organ that fills and empties with urine.
Simple columnar epithelium is a single layer of tall cells. It lines the stomach and intestines. Pick it for the lining of the digestive tract below the esophagus.
Correct. The germinal epithelium is simple cuboidal.

questions.q: Which organs are the female gonads, the organs that produce oocytes and secrete hormones?
questions.why: The ovaries are the paired, almond-shaped female gonads, one on each side of the uterus. They produce oocytes, the female sex cells, which develop inside follicles in the ovarian cortex. The ovaries also secrete hormones, so they are endocrine glands as well as reproductive organs.
notes: Correct. The ovaries produce oocytes and secrete hormones.
The greater vestibular glands sit beside the vaginal opening and secrete lubricating mucus. Choose them if the question asked which glands of the vulva produce mucus.
The uterine tubes catch the released oocyte and carry it toward the uterus, but they do not produce it. Pick them if the question asked where fertilization usually takes place.
The mammary glands are modified sweat glands in the breast that produce milk, not oocytes. Pick them if the question asked which glands are drained by lactiferous ducts.

questions.q: What is an ovarian follicle?
options: A fringe at the end of the uterine tube that sweeps the oocyte inward
A scar of connective tissue left after the corpus luteum breaks down
A fold of peritoneum that attaches the ovary to the broad ligament
A structure in the ovarian cortex holding an oocyte as it develops
questions.why: An ovarian follicle is a small structure in the cortex of the ovary, made of an oocyte surrounded by one or more layers of supporting cells. Follicles grow through stages, and at ovulation a mature follicle releases its oocyte. The follicles are always found in the cortex, while the deeper medulla holds the blood vessels and nerves.
notes: This describes the fimbriae, the finger-like projections of the infundibulum. Pick them if the question asked what sweeps the released oocyte into the uterine tube.
This describes the corpus albicans, the white scar left when a corpus luteum degenerates. Choose it if the question asked what the corpus luteum becomes.
This describes the mesovarium, the part of the broad ligament that holds the ovary. Pick it if the question asked how the broad ligament attaches to the ovary.
Correct. A follicle is an oocyte and its surrounding cells, found in the ovarian cortex.
questions.answerText: A structure in the ovarian cortex holding an oocyte as it develops

questions.q: Which list orders the stages of an ovarian follicle from earliest to most mature?
questions.why: A follicle starts as a primordial follicle, a primary oocyte with one layer of flat follicle cells. It becomes a primary follicle when those cells turn cuboidal and the zona pellucida forms, then a secondary follicle with several layers of granulosa cells and small pockets of fluid. The last stage is the vesicular (mature, Graafian) follicle, with one large fluid-filled antrum, ready to release its oocyte at ovulation.
notes: Correct. The follicle grows from primordial to primary to secondary to vesicular.
This is the right sequence written backward, from mature to earliest. It would be correct only if the question asked for the order from the most mature stage back to the start.
This puts primary before primordial. Primordial means existing from the beginning, so the primordial follicle is the starting stage; students pick this because primary also sounds like first.
This swaps primary and secondary. The follicle is primary before it becomes secondary, just as the words suggest.

questions.q: What structure is left in the ovary after ovulation, and what does it later become?
options: The corpus luteum, which later becomes a new primordial follicle
The corpus luteum, which later becomes the corpus albicans
The corpus albicans, which later becomes the corpus luteum
The vesicular follicle, which later becomes a primary follicle
questions.why: After a mature follicle releases its oocyte, the remaining follicle cells form the corpus luteum, whose name means yellow body. The corpus luteum secretes hormones for a time, and if no pregnancy occurs it degenerates. What remains is a whitish scar of connective tissue called the corpus albicans, which means white body.
notes: The corpus luteum is right, but it ends as a scar, not a new follicle. Primordial follicles are already present in the ovary and are not made from old corpora lutea.
Correct. The corpus luteum forms after ovulation and degenerates into the corpus albicans.
This reverses the sequence. The yellow body forms first and the white scar is what is left when it breaks down; students mix up which Latin color word comes first.
The vesicular follicle is the mature follicle that ruptures at ovulation, so it is the structure before ovulation, not after. Follicles never go backward to an earlier stage.
questions.answerText: The corpus luteum, which later becomes the corpus albicans

questions.q: Which ligament anchors the ovary to the uterus, and which attaches it to the pelvic wall?
options: Suspensory ligament to the uterus; ovarian ligament to the pelvic wall
Ovarian ligament to the uterus; suspensory ligament to the pelvic wall
Round ligament to the uterus; cardinal ligament to the pelvic wall
Broad ligament to the uterus; uterosacral ligament to the pelvic wall
questions.why: The ovarian ligament is a short cord that runs from the ovary medially to the side of the uterus. The suspensory ligament is a fold that runs from the ovary laterally to the pelvic wall and carries the ovarian blood vessels. Together they hold the ovary between the uterus and the side wall of the pelvis.
notes: This swaps the two ligaments. The ovarian ligament is the one that reaches the uterus, which matches its short medial path; students pick this when they forget which end each ligament attaches to.
Correct. The ovarian ligament ties the ovary to the uterus, and the suspensory ligament ties it to the pelvic wall.

The round ligament runs from the uterus to the labia majora, and the cardinal ligament runs from the pelvic wall to the cervix and vagina. Neither one holds the ovary; pick the round ligament if the question asked which ligament ends in the labia majora.

The broad ligament is a fold of peritoneum that drapes over the uterus and tubes, and the uterosacral ligament connects the uterus to the sacrum. Neither is the ovary's own tie to the uterus or the pelvic wall; choose the uterosacral ligament if the question asked what anchors the uterus to the sacrum.
questions.answerText: Ovarian ligament to the uterus; suspensory ligament to the pelvic wall

questions.q: Which structures sweep the released oocyte into the funnel of the uterine tube?
questions.why: The fimbriae are finger-like projections that fringe the infundibulum, the funnel-shaped end of the uterine tube. The infundibulum opens into the pelvic cavity rather than sealing onto the ovary. At ovulation, the fimbriae sweep over the ovary and draw the released oocyte into the tube.
notes: The ovarian ligament anchors the ovary to the uterus. It holds the ovary in place but does not catch the oocyte; pick it if the question asked which ligament ties the ovary to the uterus.

The isthmus is the narrow, thick-walled part of the tube that joins it to the uterus, at the opposite end from the ovary. Choose it if the question asked which part of the tube connects to the uterus.
Correct. The fimbriae sweep the oocyte into the infundibulum.
The ampulla is the widest and longest part of the uterine tube, past the infundibulum. Pick it if the question asked where fertilization usually takes place.

questions.q: In which part of the female reproductive tract does fertilization usually occur?
options: The ampulla of the uterine tube
The isthmus of the uterine tube
questions.why: Fertilization usually takes place in the ampulla, the widest and longest part of the uterine tube. The oocyte is swept into the tube at the infundibulum and moves into the ampulla, where sperm that have traveled up from the uterus can meet it. The early embryo then continues through the isthmus to the uterus.
notes: The uterine cavity is past the end of the tube. The oocyte reaches it only after the ampulla and isthmus, so fertilization has usually already happened by then.
Correct. The ampulla is the usual site of fertilization.
The isthmus is the narrow segment near the uterus that comes after the ampulla. Pick it if the question asked which part of the tube joins the uterus.

The infundibulum is the funnel-shaped opening of the tube, fringed with fimbriae, that the oocyte passes through before the ampulla. Choose it if the question asked which part of the tube opens into the pelvic cavity near the ovary.
questions.answerText: The ampulla of the uterine tube

questions.q: How is the oocyte moved along the uterine tube toward the uterus?
options: Pressure from the ruptured follicle pushes it
It swims with its own flagellum
Beating cilia and smooth muscle waves of the tube move it
Skeletal muscle in the tube wall squeezes it
questions.why: The oocyte cannot move on its own. The lining of the uterine tube has ciliated cells whose cilia beat toward the uterus, and a layer of smooth muscle in the wall squeezes in waves. Together they move the oocyte toward the uterus over a few days.
notes: Ovulation releases the oocyte into the pelvic cavity near the tube, but that release does not push it along the tube. Once inside, the oocyte depends on the cilia and smooth muscle of the tube.
The oocyte has no flagellum. Sperm are the cells that swim with a tail, which is the mix-up behind this choice.
Correct. Cilia beating toward the uterus and waves of smooth muscle in the wall move the oocyte.
The wall of the uterine tube has smooth muscle, not skeletal muscle, so it is never under voluntary control. Skeletal muscle would be the answer for the external urethral sphincter.
questions.answerText: Beating cilia and smooth muscle waves of the tube move it

questions.q: Which list traces an oocyte from the ovary to the uterus?
questions.why: At ovulation the oocyte leaves the ovary, and the fimbriae sweep it into the infundibulum, the funnel at the open end of the tube. It moves into the ampulla, the wide part where fertilization usually happens, then through the narrow isthmus. The isthmus joins the uterus, so the oocyte or early embryo enters the uterine cavity last.
notes: This swaps the ampulla and isthmus. The wide ampulla is closer to the ovary, and the narrow isthmus is the part that connects to the uterus.
This puts the ampulla before the funnel. The oocyte must enter the tube through the infundibulum before it can reach the ampulla.
This lists the tube regions backward, starting from the end that joins the uterus. The infundibulum is the end nearest the ovary, so it must come first.
Correct. The oocyte passes from the funnel to the wide ampulla to the narrow isthmus and into the uterus.

questions.q: Which list names the three regions of the uterus?
questions.why: The fundus is the dome-shaped top of the uterus, above where the uterine tubes enter. The body is the tapered central portion that surrounds the uterine cavity. The cervix is the narrow inferior portion that opens into the vagina.
notes: The pylorus is the outlet region of the stomach. The stomach also has a fundus and a body, which is why this mix-up is tempting; pick this set for stomach regions.
These are the three layers of the uterine wall, from outer to inner, not its regions. Choose this list if the question asked for the wall layers.
The ampulla and isthmus are regions of the uterine tube, not the uterus. Pick this set if the question asked for regions of the uterine tube, along with the infundibulum.
Correct. The uterus is divided into the fundus, body, and cervix.

questions.q: Which list names the three layers of the uterine wall from outer to inner?
questions.why: The prefixes give the order. Peri means around, so the perimetrium is the outer serous layer, part of the visceral peritoneum. Myo means muscle, so the myometrium is the thick smooth muscle middle layer, and endo means within, so the endometrium is the inner vascular lining.
notes: Correct. Around, muscle, within: perimetrium, myometrium, endometrium.
This puts the muscle on the outside, but the serous perimetrium covers the outer surface. Students choose this when they forget that peri means around.
This is the right order written from inner to outer. It would be correct if the question asked for the layers starting at the uterine cavity.
This places the lining in the middle. The endometrium lines the uterine cavity, so it must be the innermost layer.

questions.q: Which layer of the uterine wall is made of smooth muscle and is thickest in the fundus?
questions.why: The myometrium is the thick middle layer of the uterine wall, made of smooth muscle, and it is thickest in the fundus. It is the layer of the uterus that contracts during childbirth. Myo means muscle, which is the clue that this is the muscle layer.
notes: The detrusor is smooth muscle too, but it is the muscle of the urinary bladder wall, not the uterus. Pick it if the question asked which muscle contracts to empty the bladder.
The endometrium is the inner mucous lining, not a muscle layer. Pick it if the question asked which layer sheds during menstruation.
Correct. The myometrium is the smooth muscle layer of the uterus, thickest in the fundus.
The perimetrium is the thin outer serous layer, part of the visceral peritoneum, not muscle. Choose it if the question asked which layer covers the outside of the uterus.

questions.q: How is the endometrium built in two layers, and why does that matter each cycle?
options: Both strata shed each cycle and are rebuilt from the myometrium
The myometrium sheds each cycle and is rebuilt from the perimetrium
The stratum basalis sheds each cycle and is rebuilt from the stratum functionalis
The stratum functionalis sheds each cycle and is rebuilt from the stratum basalis
questions.why: The endometrium has two layers. The stratum functionalis is the thick surface layer that builds up during the cycle and is shed during menstruation. The stratum basalis is the thin, permanent deeper layer that is never shed, and it regrows a new functionalis after each period, so the lining can renew month after month.
notes: If both strata shed, the lining could not regrow. The myometrium is muscle and does not make new endometrium; the stratum basalis does that job.
The myometrium is the smooth muscle layer and the perimetrium is the outer serous layer, and neither sheds. Shedding happens only in the endometrium.
This reverses the two layers. The basalis must stay in place, because if it shed there would be nothing left to rebuild the lining from.
Correct. The functionalis is shed and the permanent basalis regrows it.
questions.answerText: The stratum functionalis sheds each cycle and is rebuilt from the stratum basalis

questions.q: Which of these structures is NOT part of the vulva, the external genitalia?
questions.why: The vulva is the external genitalia: the mons pubis, labia majora, labia minora, clitoris, and vestibule. The cervix is the narrow inferior region of the uterus, which opens into the vagina deep inside the body. Because it is part of an internal organ, it is not part of the vulva.
notes: The vestibule is the region between the labia minora that holds the vaginal and urethral openings, so it is part of the vulva. Pick it if the question asked where the urethral opening is found.
The labia minora are the smaller, hairless folds inside the labia majora and are part of the vulva. Choose them if the question asked which folds enclose the vestibule.
Correct. The cervix is part of the uterus, an internal organ, not the external genitalia.

The mons pubis is the cushion of fat over the pubic symphysis and is part of the vulva, so it does not fit a question asking for the exception. Pick it if the question asked what lies over the pubic symphysis.

questions.q: Which vulvar structures are homologous to the scrotum and to the penis?
options: Labia majora match the scrotum; the clitoris matches the penis
The vestibule matches the scrotum; the labia minora match the penis
Labia majora match the penis; the clitoris matches the scrotum
Labia minora match the scrotum; the mons pubis matches the penis
questions.why: Homologous structures develop from the same embryonic tissue in males and females. The labia majora are hair-covered folds of skin that form from the same tissue as the scrotum. The clitoris is a small mass of erectile tissue that forms from the same tissue as the penis, which is why both contain erectile tissue.
notes: Correct. The labia majora match the scrotum, and the clitoris matches the penis.

The vestibule is the space between the labia minora holding the vaginal and urethral openings, not a fold of skin like the scrotum. The erectile match for the penis is the clitoris, not the labia minora.
This swaps the pair. The clitoris is the erectile structure, so it matches the penis, and the skin folds of the labia majora match the scrotal sac.

The labia minora are the inner hairless folds, and the mons pubis is a fat pad over the pubic symphysis. Neither matches the scrotum or penis; the hair-covered outer folds, the labia majora, are the match for the scrotum.
questions.answerText: Labia majora match the scrotum; the clitoris matches the penis

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the mammary glands and how their milk reaches the nipple?
options: Endocrine glands; milk passes into the blood and then to the nipple
Modified sweat glands; the areola carries milk to the nipple
Modified sebaceous glands; suspensory ligaments carry milk to the nipple
Modified sweat glands; lactiferous ducts carry milk to the nipple
questions.why: The mammary glands are modified sweat glands that produce milk. Inside each gland, milk-secreting alveoli sit in lobules, the lobules sit in lobes, and each lobe drains through lactiferous ducts that open at the nipple. Naming them in that order also names the path the milk takes.
notes: Mammary glands are exocrine glands, meaning they release their product through ducts onto a surface rather than into the blood. Choose endocrine if the question were about a ductless gland that releases hormones into the blood.
The areola is the ring of pigmented skin around the nipple; it carries no milk. Pick it if the question asked which circular area of skin surrounds the nipple.

Sebaceous glands secrete oil into hair follicles, and the suspensory (Cooper's) ligaments support the breast rather than carry milk. Pick the suspensory ligaments if the question asked what supports the breast tissue.
Correct. Mammary glands are modified sweat glands drained by lactiferous ducts.
questions.answerText: Modified sweat glands; lactiferous ducts carry milk to the nipple

questions.q: An ovary slide shows an oocyte ringed by several layers of granulosa cells, with a theca outside and small pockets of fluid between the cells, but no single large cavity. Which stage is this, and what stage comes next?
options: A primordial follicle, which becomes a primary follicle
A mature follicle, which ruptures at ovulation
A primary follicle, which becomes a secondary follicle
A secondary follicle, which becomes a mature follicle
questions.why: Follicle stages are named by size, layers of cells, and whether there is a fluid space. A secondary follicle has several layers of granulosa cells, a theca around the outside, and small pockets of fluid between the granulosa cells. When those pockets become one large fluid-filled cavity, the antrum, the follicle is a mature (vesicular) follicle.
notes: A primordial follicle is the smallest stage, a primary oocyte with one layer of flat follicle cells. It has no granulosa layers, theca, or fluid.
A mature follicle has one large antrum and bulges from the ovary surface. Small scattered fluid pockets with no single cavity mean it is not there yet.
